upaparvas.title: Table of Contents Parva
chapters: 1- The introduction of the book, a brief list of most of the topics mentioned in the book, and the glory of its text.

upaparvas.title: Parva Collection Parva
chapters: 2- Description of the Samantapanchak region, details about the Akshauhini army, a collection of the parvas (books) and their brief topics described in the Mahabharata, and the benefits of listening to and reading the Mahabharata.

upaparvas.title: Paushya Parva
chapters: 3- Sarama's curse to Janamejaya, Janamejaya appointing Somashrava as priest, the guru devotion of Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda, and Uttanka, and Uttanka encouraging Janamejaya to perform the snake sacrifice (Sarpayajna).

upaparvas.title: Pauloma Parva
chapters: 4- Beginning of the story
5- Arrival of the demon Pauloma at Bhrigu's ashram and his conversation with Agni (the fire god)
6- Birth of sage Chyavana, Pauloma demon being reduced to ashes by his radiance, and Bhrigu cursing Agni
7- Agni, angered by the curse, becomes invisible, and Brahma pleases him by limiting the curse
8- Birth of Pramadvara, her betrothal to Ruru, and her death by snakebite before marriage
9- Pramadvara coming back to life after Ruru gives up half his lifespan, their marriage, Ruru's resolve to kill snakes, and the dialogue between Ruru and Dundubhi
10- Dialogue between Ruru Muni and Dundubhi
11- Dundubhi's life story and his teaching of non-violence to Ruru
12- Ruru's curiosity about Janamejaya's snake sacrifice and his father fulfilling that curiosity

upaparvas.title: Astika Parva
chapters: 13- Jaratkaru, at the request of his ancestors, decides to marry
14- Jaratkaru marries Vasuki’s sister
15- Birth of Astika and, due to his mother’s curse, Astika saves the Naga race from destruction in the snake sacrifice
16- Kadru and Vinata receive their desired children through Kashyapa’s boon
17- On Mount Meru, Lord Narayana instructs the gods planning for nectar to churn the ocean
18- Churning of the ocean by the gods and demons for nectar, emergence of many gems and nectar, and Lord Vishnu taking the Mohini form to recover the nectar from the demons
19- The gods drink nectar, Deva-Asura battle, and the victory of the gods
20- Contest between Kadru and Vinata, Kadru cursing her sons, and Brahma approving the curse
21- Detailed description of the ocean
22- The serpents blacken the tail of Uchchaihshravas; Kadru and Vinata move forward while seeing the ocean
23- Defeated Vinata becomes Kadru’s slave, birth of Garuda, and his praise by the gods
24- Garuda reduces his radiance and size, and Aruna sits on his chariot to calm the intense heat from Surya’s anger
25- Kadru praises Indra to protect the snakes who have fainted from Surya’s heat
26- The snakes rejoice as Indra brings rain
27- Description of the beautiful forest of Ramaniyaka island, and Garuda asks the snakes how he can be freed from servitude
28- Garuda goes in search of nectar and, as per his mother’s order, devours the Nishadas
29- Kashyapa tells Garuda the story of the previous lives of the elephant and the tortoise; Garuda carries both to a divine banyan branch, and about that branch...
30- Garuda meets Kashyapa, the Valakhilya sages leave the branch to practice austerity upon his prayer, and Garuda drops the branch on a deserted mountain city
31- Indra insults the Valakhilyas, and from their penance, Aruna and Garuda are born
32- Garuda battles the gods and defeats them
33- Garuda returns with the nectar, receives a boon from Lord Vishnu on the way, and Indra strikes him with the Vajra (thunderbolt)
34- Friendship between Indra and Garuda, Garuda brings nectar to the Nagas and frees Vinata from slavery, and Indra steals the nectar
35- Names of the prominent Nagas
36- Shesha Naga’s penance, receiving a boon from Brahma, and bearing the Earth on his head
37- Nagas, including Vasuki, consult each other to avoid their mother’s curse
38- Vasuki’s sister decides to marry the sage Jaratkaru
39- At Brahma’s command, Vasuki tries to marry his sister to Jaratkaru
40- Jaratkaru’s penance, story of King Parikshit, and Krisha becomes upset by the king putting a dead snake on the sage’s shoulder, prompting Shringa
41- Sage Shringa curses King Parikshit, and Shamik tries to calm his son and explains the curse is inappropriate
42- Shamik explains to his son and sends Gaurmukh to King Parikshit, the king arranges for his own protection, and Takshaka the serpent talks with Kashyapa
43- Takshaka bribes Kashyapa to turn back, and then secretly approaches the king and bites him
44- Janamejaya’s coronation and marriage
45- Jaratkaru meets his ancestors and speaks with them
46- Jaratkaru agrees to marry under certain conditions, and King Vasuki brings his sister named Jaratkaru
47- Sage Jaratkaru marries the Naga maiden, the Naga maiden serves her husband, and her husband leaves for austerity
48- Vasuki worries, his sister reassures him, Astika is born and learns the scriptures
49- Virtuous conduct and noble qualities of King Parikshit, his going hunting, and his insulting of Sage Shamik
50- Shringa curses Parikshit, Takshaka turns back Kashyapa and bites Parikshit in disguise, and upon hearing of his father’s death, Janamejaya vows to take revenge on Takshaka
51- Janamejaya initiates the snake sacrifice
52- Beginning of the snake sacrifice and destruction of many snakes
53- Names of the priests performing the snake sacrifice, the terrible destruction of snakes, Takshaka seeks refuge with Indra, and Vasuki asks his sister to send Astika to the sacrifice
54- On his mother’s orders, Astika consoles his uncle and goes to the snake sacrifice
55- Astika praises the patron, the sacrifice, the priests, the members, and Agni
56- The king prepares to grant Astika a boon, Takshaka is distressed, and Astika asks for a boon
57- Names of the chief snakes burned in the sacrifice
58- Conclusion of the sacrifice and Astika receives a boon from the snakes

upaparvas.title: Anshavatarana Parva
chapters: 59- Beginning of the Mahabharata
60- Arrival of Vyasa at Janamejaya’s sacrifice, his welcome, and at the king’s request, Vyasa instructs Vaishampayana to narrate the Mahabharata story
61- Brief outline of the discord between the Kauravas and Pandavas and the events leading to war
62- The greatness of the Mahabharata
63- The story of King Uparichara, and the brief birth stories of Satyavati, Vyasa, and other main characters

64- Origin and growth of the Kshatriya lineage by the Brahmins, description of the religious kingdom of that era, the birth of the Asuras (demons), the earth burdened by them seeking refuge with Brahma, and Brahma instructing the gods to incarnate on earth

upaparvas.title: Sambhava Parva
chapters: 65- Description of the lineage of sages like Marichi and the daughters of Daksha like Aditi
66- Description of the progeny of sages and the wives of Kashyapa
67- Overview of the partial incarnations of gods, demons, and others
68- Description of King Dushyanta’s remarkable power and administrative abilities
69- Dushyanta goes hunting in the forest and kills various wild animals
70- Description of the hermitage and Kanva’s ashram, and King Dushyanta’s arrival there
71- Conversation between King Dushyanta and Shakuntala; Shakuntala explains the reason for her birth, and Indra, worried by Vishwamitra’s penance, sends Menaka to disturb his austerities
72- Menaka and Vishwamitra’s union, the birth of their daughter, her protection by Shakun birds, and Kanva bringing her to his hermitage and naming her Shakuntala
73- Gandharva marriage of Shakuntala and Dushyanta, and Sage Kanva’s approval

74- Birth of Shakuntala’s son, his extraordinary power, Shakuntala going to Dushyanta with her son, Dushyanta–Shakuntala dialogue, the celestial voice affirming Shakuntala’s purity, and Bharata’s coronation
75- Origin of Daksha, Vaivasvata Manu and their sons; brief accounts of Pururava, Nahusha, and Yayati
76- Kacha serving Shukracharya and Devayani as a disciple, enduring many hardships and obtaining the knowledge of reviving the dead
77- Devayani requests Kacha for marriage, Kacha refuses, and they both curse each other
78- Conflict between Devayani and Sharmishtha, Sharmishtha throws Devayani into a well, Yayati rescues her, and Devayani converses with Shukracharya
79- Shukracharya tries to pacify Devayani, but she remains dissatisfied
80- Shukracharya rebukes Vrishaparva and prepares to leave, but at Vrishaparva’s command, Sharmishtha becomes Devayani’s maid to appease Shukracharya and Devayani
81- Devayani and Sharmishtha’s forest excursion with friends, arrival of King Yayati, Devayani’s conversation with him, and their marriage
82- Devayani bears a son with Yayati; Yayati’s union with Sharmishtha in private results in a son
83- Dialogue between Devayani and Sharmishtha; upon learning of Sharmishtha’s son by Yayati, Devayani becomes upset and goes to her father; Shukracharya curses Yayati with old age

84- Yayati requests his sons Yadu, Turvasu, Druhyu, and Anu to exchange their youth for his old age, but when they refuse, he curses them; then he exchanges old age for youth with his son Puru and grants him a boon
85- King Yayati’s indulgence in worldly pleasures, his renunciation, and Puru’s coronation before retiring to the forest
86- Yayati’s penance in the forest and his ascent to heaven
87- At Indra’s inquiry, Yayati discusses the teachings he imparted to his son Puru
88- Yayati’s fall from heaven and Astaka’s questions to him
89- Dialogue between Yayati and Astaka
90- Further conversation between Astaka and Yayati
91- Discussion between Yayati and Astaka about hermitage duties
92- Further dialogue between Astaka and Yayati; Yayati refuses the merit given by others
93- King Yayati refuses gifts from Vasuman and Shibi and goes to heaven with Astaka and three other kings
94- Description of the Puru dynasty
95- Description of the lineages from Daksha Prajapati through the Puru, Bharata, and Pandu dynasties
96- Brahma’s curse to Mahabhisha and Ganga’s conversation with the cursed Vasus
97- King Pratipa accepts Ganga as his future daughter-in-law, birth of Shantanu, his coronation, and meeting with Ganga
38- Relationship between Shantanu and Ganga with certain conditions, birth and redemption of the Vasus from their curse, and the birth of Bhishma
99- Story of the Vasus being cursed by Sage Vashistha
100- Praise for Shantanu’s appearance, qualities, and virtues, Ganga educates her son, and Devavrata takes the vow that makes him Bhishma
201- Birth of Chitrangada and Vichitravirya from Satyavati, deaths of Shantanu and Chitrangada, and Vichitravirya’s coronation

202- Bhishma abducts the daughters of the King of Kashi from their swayamvara, defeats all the other kings and Shalva in battle, marries Ambika and Ambalika to Vichitravirya, and Vichitravirya’s death
103- Satyavati requests Bhishma to take the throne and produce progeny; Bhishma refuses because of his vow
204- With Bhishma’s consent, Satyavati invites Vyasa, who, by his mother’s command, agrees to produce heirs for the Kuru dynasty through the wives of Vichitravirya
105- Vyasa begets Dhritarashtra, Pandu, and Vidura through the wives of Vichitravirya
106- Sage Mandavya is impaled on a stake
107- Mandavya curses the god of justice (Dharma)
108- Birth of Dhritarashtra and others, and Kuru country prospers under Bhishma’s righteous rule
109- Marriage of King Dhritarashtra

111- Kunti chooses Pandu at her swayamvara and marries him
112- Pandu marries Madri and conquers the directions
113- King Pandu lives in the forest with his wives; Vidura’s marriage
114- Dhritarashtra has one hundred sons and a daughter from Gandhari, and another son Yuyutsu from a servant woman
115- Story of Duhshala’s birth
116- Names of Dhritarashtra’s hundred sons
117- King Pandu kills a sage disguised as a deer and is cursed
118- Pandu’s repentance, decision to become an ascetic, and entering the hermitage at his wives’ request
119- Pandu instructs Kunti to try for children
120- Kunti narrates the story of Bhadra, wife of Vyushitaswa, who bore a son from her husband’s corpse
121- Pandu explains to Kunti and, at his command, she invokes Yama for a son
122- Birth of Yudhishthira, Bhima, and Arjuna
123- Birth of Nakula and Sahadeva, and the naming ceremony of the Pandava princes
124- King Pandu’s death and Madri’s self-immolation
125- Sages take Kunti and the Pandavas to Hastinapura and hand them over to Bhishma and others
126- Cremation of Pandu and Madri’s remains and the offering of water by relatives
127- Childhood games of the Pandavas and sons of Dhritarashtra; Duryodhana tries to poison Bhima and push him into the Ganga, Bhima drinks the divine nectar in the Naga realm
128- Kunti and others worry when Bhima does not return, Bhima comes back from the Naga realm, and Duryodhana’s further mischief
129- Birth of Kripacharya, Drona, and Ashwatthama; Drona receives weapons from Parashurama
130- Drona, insulted by Drupada, comes to Hastinapura, meets the princes, retrieves their ball and ring from a well, and Bhishma honors him
131- Dronacharya trains the princes, Ekalavya’s devotion to his guru, and...
132- Arjuna’s archery feat, Drona’s release from the crocodile, and Arjuna receives the Brahmashira weapon
133- The princes demonstrate their skill in archery in the arena
134- Bhima, Duryodhana, and Arjuna demonstrate their weapon skills
135- Karna enters the arena and is crowned
136- Bhima insults Karna, and Duryodhana honors him
137- Drona sends his pupils to attack Drupada, Arjuna captures Drupada, and Drona frees him after giving him half the kingdom
138- Yudhishthira is appointed crown prince; Dhritarashtra worries about the Pandavas’ growing fame, glory, and strength
139- Kanika gives Dhritarashtra advice on politics

upaparvas.title: Jatugriha Parva
chapters: 140- Duryodhana’s concern upon seeing the citizens’ affection for the Pandavas
141- Duryodhana proposes to Dhritarashtra to send the Pandavas to Varanavata
142- The Pandavas depart for Varanavata on Dhritarashtra's orders
143- Under Duryodhana’s command, Purochana builds the house of lac in the city of Varanavata
144- The Pandavas travel to Varanavata and receive Vidura’s secret advice

147- The burning of the house of lac and the Pandavas’ escape through the tunnel
148- The boatman sent by Vidura ferries the Pandavas across the Ganga
149- Dhritarashtra and others grieve for the Pandavas, perform funeral rites, and the Pandavas enter the forest
150- Bhima fetches water for mother Kunti, feels sorrow seeing his mother and brothers sleeping on the ground, and grows angry at Duryodhana

upaparvas.title: Hidimba-vadha Parva
chapters: 151- At Hidimba’s urging, the demoness Hidimbaa approaches the Pandavas and converses with Bhima
152- Hidimba arrives, Hidimbaa becomes frightened of him, and a battle ensues between Bhima and the demon Hidimbasura
153- Hidimbaa expresses her feelings to Kunti and others; Bhima kills Hidimbasura
154- Yudhishthira stops Bhima from killing Hidimbaa, and Hidimbaa’s devotion to Bhima
155- The Pandavas meet Sage Vyasa and enter the city of Ekachakra

upaparvas.title: Baka-vadha Parva
chapters: 156- Kunti discusses with Bhima to relieve a Brahmin family's distress and the Brahmin expresses his deep worries
157- The Brahmin’s wife prepares to sacrifice herself and requests her husband to stay alive
158- The Brahmin’s daughter’s renunciation and wise words, and Kunti approaches them all
159- On Kunti’s inquiry, the Brahmin explains the reason for their suffering
160- Conversation between Kunti and the Brahmin
161- Discussion between Yudhishthira and Kunti about sending Bhima to the demon
162- Bhima takes food to Bakasura, eats himself, and after a fight, kills the demon
163- After Bakasura’s death, the demons flee in fear and the townspeople rejoice

upaparvas.title: Chaitraratha Parva
chapters: 164- The Pandavas hear strange tales from a Brahmin
165- The account of Drona being insulted by Drupada
166- Birth of Dhrishtadyumna and Draupadi from Drupada’s sacrifice
167- Kunti consults her sons and prepares to go to Panchala
168- Vyasa narrates Draupadi’s story from her previous birth to the Pandavas
169- The Pandavas travel to Panchala; Arjuna defeats the Gandharva Chitraratha and they become friends
170- King Samvarana is captivated upon seeing Surya’s daughter Tapati
171- Conversation between Tapati and Samvarana
172- With Sage Vasishtha’s help, King Samvarana attains Tapati
173- The Gandharva urges the appointment of a worthy Brahmin as priest, praising Vasishtha’s greatness
174- Vishwamitra is defeated before Vasishtha’s amazing power of forgiveness
175- By Shakti’s curse, Kalmashapada becomes a demon; prompted by Vishwamitra, the demon devours Vasishtha’s sons, and Vasishtha grieves
176- Kalmashapada is freed from his curse and, through Vasishtha, obtains a son named Ashmaka
177- Birth of Parashara, son of Shakti; Vasishtha tells the Aurva story to calm Parashara’s anger upon hearing of his father’s death
178- The ancestors pacify Aurva’s anger
179- Conversation between Aurva and the ancestors; Aurva casts his fiery rage into the ocean as the submarine fire
180- Sage Parashara, persuaded by Pulastya and other sages, ends the sacrificial killing of demons
181- The Brahmin woman Angirasi curses King Kalmashapada
182- The Pandavas appoint Dhaumya as their priest

upaparvas.title: Swayamvara Parva
chapters: 183- The Pandavas journey to Panchala and converse with Brahmins along the way
184- The Pandavas stay with a potter in Drupada’s capital, description of the Swayamvara assembly, and Dhrishtadyumna’s announcement
185- Dhrishtadyumna introduces the kings present at Draupadi’s Swayamvara
186- The kings attempt to hit the target and fail
187- Arjuna hits the target and wins Draupadi
188- Bhima and Arjuna prepare to face the kings intent on attacking Drupada, and Lord Krishna discusses the matter with Balarama
189- Arjuna and Bhima defeat Karna and Shalya, and then return to their quarters with Draupadi
190- Conversation between Kunti, Arjuna, and Yudhishthira; the five Pandavas consider marrying Draupadi, and Balarama and Krishna meet the Pandavas
191- Dhrishtadyumna, in disguise, observes everything and reports to King Drupada, who questions him about Draupadi

upaparvas.title: Vivaahika Parva
chapters: 192- Upon hearing of Draupadi and the Pandavas from Dhrishtadyumna, King Drupada sends his priest to them; conversation between the priest and Yudhishthira
193- The Pandavas and Kunti are honored at Drupada’s house and King Drupada tests the character of the Pandavas
194- Conversation between Drupada and Yudhishthira, and the arrival of Sage Vyasa
195- In Vyasa’s presence, Drupada, Dhrishtadyumna, and Yudhishthira share their views about Draupadi marrying five men
196- Vyasa narrates the Pandavas’ and Draupadi’s past lives to Drupada, gives him divine vision, and Drupada beholds their divine forms
197- Draupadi’s marriage to all five Pandavas
198- Kunti’s advice and blessings to Draupadi, and Lord Krishna sends gifts for the Pandavas

upaparvas.title: Vidura-Agamana-Rajya-Lambha Parva
chapters: 199- Duryodhana and others worry after the Pandavas’ marriage; Dhritarashtra pretends affection for the Pandavas while Duryodhana plots
200- Conversation between Dhritarashtra and Duryodhana, discussing ways to subdue their enemies
201- Karna agrees to suppress the Pandavas by force
202- Bhishma advises Duryodhana to give half the kingdom to the Pandavas
203- Dronacharya agrees to send gifts and invite the Pandavas, and rebukes Karna for opposing this
204- Vidura supports Drona and Bhishma’s statements
205- On Dhritarashtra’s order, Vidura visits Drupada and proposes the Pandavas’ move to Hastinapura
206- The Pandavas arrive at Hastinapura, receive half the kingdom, build the city of Indraprastha, and Lord Krishna and Balarama depart for Dwaraka

208- Sunda and Upasunda perform austerities, are granted boons by Brahma, and the demons celebrate
209- Sunda and Upasunda conquer the three worlds with their cruel deeds
210- Creation of Tilottama, her captivating beauty, and her departure to enchant Sunda and Upasunda
211- Sunda and Upasunda, infatuated by Tilottama, fight each other and die; Tilottama receives a boon from Brahma, and the Pandavas set rules regarding Draupadi

upaparvas.title: Arjuna-Vanavasa Parva
chapters: 212- Arjuna violates the rule to protect a Brahmin’s cows and departs for the forest
213- Arjuna stays at Gangadwara and there meets Ulupi
214- Arjuna visits the holy places in the east, marries Chitrangada in Manipura, and has a son with her
215- Arjuna rescues the apsara Varga from the form of a crocodile and begins hearing Varga’s story
216- At Varga’s request, Arjuna frees the other four apsaras from their curses, then travels to Manipura, meets Chitrangada, and proceeds to the sacred Gokarna
217- Arjuna meets Krishna at Prabhasa Tirtha and, with him, visits Raivataka Mountain and the city of Dwaraka

upaparvas.title: Subhadra-harana Parva
chapters: 218- At the festival on Raivataka Mountain, Arjuna becomes attracted to Subhadra and, with Krishna and Yudhishthira’s consent, decides to abduct her
219- The Yadavas prepare for battle and Balarama expresses his anger towards Arjuna

upaparvas.title: Haranaharaṇa Parva
chapters: 220- Arjuna and Subhadra’s marriage in Dwaraka; after Arjuna returns to Indraprastha, Krishna and others visit with dowry; the birth, naming, and education of Draupadi’s sons and Abhimanyu

upaparvas.title: Khandava-daha Parva
chapters: 221- The uniqueness of Yudhishthira’s reign, Krishna and Arjuna go to the Khandava forest, and Agni appears to them in the guise of a Brahmin
222- Agni requests Krishna and Arjuna’s help to burn the Khandava forest, and narrates the story of King Shvetaki to explain why he wants to burn it

224- Agni grants Arjuna and Krishna a divine bow, inexhaustible quivers, a celestial chariot, and discus; with their help, Agni sets the Khandava forest ablaze
225- The suffering of the creatures trapped in the burning Khandava forest and Indra’s attempt to extinguish the fire by causing rain
226- Krishna and Arjuna battle the gods and others

upaparvas.title: Maya Darshana Parva
chapters: 227- The defeat of the gods, destruction of the Khandava forest, and the rescue of Mayasura
228- The tale of Sharngaka—Muni Mandapala’s union with Jarita and Sharngika, the birth of their sons, and the sage’s praise of Agni to save them
229- Jarita laments in worry to protect her children
230- Conversation between Jarita and her children
231- Agni, pleased by the prayers of the Sharngakas, grants them safety
232- Mandapala reunites with his family
233- Indra grants boons to Krishna and Arjuna; Krishna, Arjuna, and Mayasura bid farewell to Agni and sit together on the banks of the Yamuna

upaparvas.title: Sabha-Kriya Parva
chapters: 1- Following Lord Krishna’s command, Mayasura prepares to build the assembly hall
2- Lord Krishna’s journey to Dwaraka
3- Mayasura presents Bhima with a mace and Arjuna with a conch, and constructs the marvelous assembly hall
4- Dharmaraja Yudhishthira enters the hall built by Maya, with a description of the sages and kings present in the assembly

upaparvas.title: Lokapala Sabhakhyana Parva
chapters: 5- Sage Narada arrives in Yudhishthira’s assembly and offers guidance to Yudhishthira through questions
6- Yudhishthira inquires about the divine assemblies
7- Description of Indra’s assembly
8- Description of Yama’s assembly
9- Description of Varuna’s assembly
10- Description of Kubera’s assembly
11- Description of Brahma’s assembly
12- The greatness of King Harishchandra and King Pandu’s message to Yudhishthira

upaparvas.title: Rajasuyarambha Parva
chapters: 13- Yudhishthira’s resolve to perform the Rajasuya sacrifice and his consultations with his brothers, ministers, sages, and Krishna
14- Krishna’s approval for the Rajasuya Yajna
15- Conversation between Yudhishthira, Bhima, and Krishna about Jarasandha
16- When Yudhishthira hesitates to confront Jarasandha, Arjuna encourages him with spirited words
17- Krishna agrees with Arjuna and narrates to Yudhishthira the story of Jarasandha’s birth
18- The demoness Jara introduces herself, and the child is named after her
19- Sage Chandakaushika foretells Jarasandha’s future; his father anoints him king and retires to the forest

upaparvas.title: Jarasandha-vadha Parva
chapters: 20- With Yudhishthira’s approval, Krishna, Arjuna, and Bhima set out for Magadha
21- Krishna praises the capital of Magadha; the three break through Chaityaka hill and the city’s drums, enter the city and royal palace; dialogue between Krishna and Jarasandha
22- Conversation between Jarasandha and Krishna; Jarasandha prepares for battle and explains his enmity with Krishna
23- Jarasandha decides to duel Bhima; a fierce battle between Bhima and Jarasandha, leading to Jarasandha’s exhaustion

upaparvas.title: Digvijaya Parva
chapters: 25- Arjuna and the other three brothers set out on their conquests in different directions
26- Arjuna defeats many kingdoms and kings, including Bhagadatta
27- Arjuna conquers various mountainous regions
28- Arjuna conquers Kimpurusha, Hataka, and Uttarakuru, then returns to Indraprastha
29- Bhima departs to conquer the eastern direction and defeats many kingdoms
30- Bhima returns to Indraprastha with great wealth after conquering many eastern kingdoms and kings
31- Sahadeva conquers the southern direction
32- Nakula conquers the western direction

upaparvas.title: Rajasuyaparva
chapters: 33- The excellence of Yudhishthira’s rule, at Krishna’s command Yudhishthira undertakes the Rajasuya Yajna, and invitations are sent to kings, Brahmins, and relatives

35- Description of the Rajasuya Yajna

upaparvas.title: Arghabhi-harana Parva
chapters: 36- Gathering of Brahmins and kings at the Rajasuya Yajna; Sage Narada describes Krishna’s greatness and, with Bhishma’s consent, Krishna is given the chief honor
37- Shishupala’s words of accusation
38- Yudhishthira tries to reason with Shishupala, and Bhishma responds to his accusations
39- Sahadeva challenges the assembled kings, and the enraged Shishupala and other kings prepare for battle

upaparvas.title: Shishupala-vadha Parva
chapters: 40- Yudhishthira’s worry and Bhishma’s reassurance
41- Shishupala insults Bhishma
42- Bhima grows angry at Shishupala’s words, and Bhishma calms him
43- Bhishma narrates the story of Shishupala’s birth
44- Shishupala, irritated by Bhishma’s words, rebukes him; Bhishma challenges all the kings to fight Krishna
45- Krishna slays Shishupala, the Rajasuya Yajna concludes, and all the Brahmins, kings, and Krishna return to their homelands

upaparvas.title: Dyuta Parva
chapters: 46- Yudhishthira is troubled by Vyasa’s prophecy and vows to maintain equanimity
47- Duryodhana visits the Mayasura-built hall, becomes the subject of ridicule due to illusions at every step, and grows anxious seeing Yudhishthira’s prosperity
48- Shakuni and Duryodhana plot to defeat the Pandavas
49- Duryodhana shares his worries with Dhritarashtra, requests a game of dice, and Dhritarashtra orders Vidura to go to Indraprastha
50- Duryodhana explains the reasons for his sorrow and anxiety to Dhritarashtra
51- The subject of Duryodhana’s distress
52- Duryodhana describes the gifts received by Yudhishthira
53- Duryodhana describes Yudhishthira’s consecration
54- Dhritarashtra tries to counsel Duryodhana
55- Duryodhana incites Dhritarashtra
56- Conversation between Dhritarashtra and Duryodhana; the assembly is prepared for the dice game, and Dhritarashtra orders Vidura to summon Yudhishthira
57- Conversation between Vidura and Dhritarashtra
58- Conversation between Vidura and Yudhishthira, and Yudhishthira’s arrival in Hastinapura and meeting with everyone
59- Dialogue between Yudhishthira and Shakuni about the impropriety of gambling
60- The dice game begins
61- With Shakuni’s deceit, Yudhishthira loses every bet
62- Vidura warns Dhritarashtra
63- Vidura strongly opposes the dice game
64- Duryodhana rebukes Vidura, and Vidura warns him
65- Yudhishthira loses his wealth, kingdom, brothers, Draupadi, and finally himself
66- Vidura rebukes Duryodhana
67- When Draupadi refuses to come upon being summoned, Dushasana drags her by the hair into the assembly; Draupadi questions the assembly

68- Bhima’s rage and Arjuna calming him; Vikarna’s just words opposed by Karna, Draupadi’s disrobing and Krishna’s miraculous protection of her modesty; Vidura inspires the assembly to protest by citing Prahlada’s example
69- Draupadi’s warning-filled lament and Bhishma’s response
70- Duryodhana’s deceitful words and Bhima’s angry vow
71- Words of Karna and Duryodhana, Bhima’s oath, Vidura’s warning, and Draupadi receives boons from Dhritarashtra
72- Yudhishthira calms the furious Bhima, who is ready to strike the enemy
73- Dhritarashtra returns everything to Yudhishthira, counsels him, and orders him to return to Indraprastha

upaparvas.title: Anudyuta Parva
chapters: 74- Duryodhana describes Arjuna’s valor to Dhritarashtra and requests the Pandavas be called again for another dice game; the Pandavas agree
75- Gandhari warns Dhritarashtra, but he refuses to listen
76- Despite everyone’s objections, Yudhishthira, at Dhritarashtra’s command, gambles again and loses
77- Dushasana mocks the Pandavas; Bhima, Arjuna, Nakula, and Sahadeva make fierce vows to destroy their enemies
78- Yudhishthira bids farewell to Dhritarashtra and others; Vidura proposes to keep Kunti with him and advises the Pandavas to uphold righteousness
79- Draupadi bids farewell to Kunti; Kunti laments, and the people of the city are filled with sorrow
80- The Pandavas’ actions as they depart for the forest, the sorrow of the citizens; conversation between Dhritarashtra and Vidura, and Dronacharya reassures the Kauravas who seek refuge
81- Dhritarashtra’s anxiety and his conversation with Sanjaya

upaparvas.title: Aranya Parva
chapters: 1- The Pandavas depart for the forest, followed by the townspeople; at Yudhishthira’s request, many return, and the Pandavas spend the night at Pramanakoti Tirtha
2- Conversation between Yudhishthira and Brahmins, including Shaunaka, about the faults of wealth, the importance of hospitality, and methods for well-being
3- Yudhishthira worships Lord Surya for food and receives the Akshaya Patra
4- Vidura gives wise counsel to Dhritarashtra, who becomes upset and retreats to his palace
5- The Pandavas enter the Kamyaka forest; Vidura visits and converses with them
6- Dhritarashtra sends Sanjaya to bring Vidura back from the forest and seeks his forgiveness
7- Duryodhana, Dushasana, Shakuni, and Karna conspire to kill the Pandavas and prepare to go to the forest, but Vyasa intervenes and stops them
8- Vyasa urges Dhritarashtra to restrain Duryodhana’s injustice
9- Vyasa narrates the story of Surabhi and Indra, showing compassion toward the Pandavas
10- After Vyasa leaves, Maitreya requests Dhritarashtra and Duryodhana to be kind to the Pandavas; offended by Duryodhana’s rudeness, Maitreya curses him

upaparvas.title: Kirmira-vadha Parva
chapters: 11- The story of Bhima slaying Kirmira

upaparvas.title: Arjunabhigamana Parva
chapters: 12- Arjuna and Draupadi praise Lord Krishna; Draupadi describes her humiliation and suffering to Krishna, and Krishna, Arjuna, and Dhrishtadyumna reassure her
13- Krishna explains the faults of gambling and considers his own absence as the reason for the Pandavas’ misfortune
14- Krishna briefly describes his battle with Shalva during the dice game and the destruction of Shalva’s airship
15- In the context of Shalva’s defeat, the defensive preparations in Dwaraka are described
16- The Yadava army resists Shalva’s massive attack; Samba defeats Kshemavriddhi, Vegavan is killed, Charudeshna slays Vivindhyaditya, and Pradyumna reassures the army
17- Fierce battle between Pradyumna and Shalva
18- After Pradyumna is carried from the battlefield while unconscious, he laments and rebukes his charioteer
19- Pradyumna defeats Shalva
20- Krishna and Shalva engage in a fierce duel
21- Krishna is initially fooled by Shalva’s illusion but regains awareness
22- Conclusion of the tale of Shalva’s defeat; Krishna, Dhrishtadyumna, and the other kings return to their cities with Yudhishthira’s permission
23- The Pandavas prepare to go to the Dvaita forest and the people’s distress
24- The Pandavas go to the Dvaita forest
25- Sage Markandeya instructs the Pandavas in righteousness and departs northward
26- Dalbhaputra Baka explains to Yudhishthira the importance of Brahmins
27- Draupadi’s sorrowful words to Yudhishthira, attempting to incite his anger toward their enemies
28- Draupadi narrates the Prahlada-Bali dialogue—when to use power and when to show forgiveness
29- Yudhishthira criticizes anger and praises forgiveness
30- Draupadi, distraught, questions Yudhishthira’s wisdom, virtue, and faith in divine justice
31- Yudhishthira answers Draupadi’s accusations, explaining the benefits of respecting God, dharma, and great souls, and the harm of disrespecting them
32- Draupadi insists on the primacy of human effort and urges Yudhishthira to act
33- Bhima praises human effort and urges Yudhishthira, as a Kshatriya, to wage war
34- Yudhishthira, citing dharma and ethics, declares his resolution to keep his promise and stick to righteousness
35- A sorrowful Bhima tries to motivate Yudhishthira for war
36- Yudhishthira consoles Bhima, Vyasa arrives and grants Yudhishthira the knowledge of Pratismriti, and the Pandavas return again to the Kamyaka forest
37- Arjuna, having reunited with his brothers, goes to Indrakila mountain and has a vision of Indra

upaparvas.title: Kairata Parva
chapters: 38- Arjuna’s intense penance and the sages’ discussion with Lord Shiva about it
39- Battle between Lord Shiva and Arjuna; Shiva is pleased with Arjuna, and Arjuna praises Shiva
40- Lord Shiva grants Arjuna a boon and returns to his abode
41- The guardians of the directions (Dikpalas) visit Arjuna, grant him divine weapons, and Indra commands Arjuna to come to heaven

upaparvas.title: Indralokabhigamana Parva
chapters: 42- Arjuna departs from the Himalayas with Matali and sets out for the heavenly realm
43- Arjuna meets Indra and is welcomed into Indra’s court
44- Arjuna receives training in weaponry and music
45- Conversation between Chitrasena and Urvashi
46- Urvashi, overcome by desire, approaches Arjuna; when he rejects her, she curses him and returns
47- Sage Lomasha meets Indra and Arjuna in heaven, takes their message, and comes to the Kamyaka forest
48- Grieving Dhritarashtra expresses concern for his sons to Sanjaya
49- Sanjaya agrees with Dhritarashtra’s concerns, and Dhritarashtra is filled with sorrow
50- The Pandavas’ sustenance in the forest
51- Sanjaya narrates to Dhritarashtra the vows made by Krishna and others to slay Duryodhana and his allies

upaparvas.title: Nalopakhyana Parva
chapters: 52- Dialogue between Bhima and Yudhishthira; arrival of Brihadashva; upon Yudhishthira’s inquiry, Brihadashva introduces the tale of Nala
53- Description of the virtues of Nala and Damayanti, their mutual love, and the swan delivering their messages to each other
54- Narada and Indra converse in heaven; kings and Lokapalas depart for Damayanti’s swayamvara
55- Nala goes as an emissary to the royal palace and delivers the gods’ message to Damayanti
56- Nala converses with Damayanti and brings her response to the gods
57- At the swayamvara, Damayanti chooses Nala; the gods bless Nala; the gods and kings depart; Nala and Damayanti marry, Nala performs sacrifices, and they have children
58- The gods praise Nala’s virtues; despite their warnings, Kali Yuga becomes hostile to Nala
59- Kali Yuga enters Nala; Nala and Pushkara play dice; despite warnings from his people and Damayanti, the king does not stop gambling
60- Sorrowful Damayanti sends her son and daughter to Kundinapura through Varshneya
61- Nala loses in dice and departs for the forest with Damayanti; birds snatch away Nala’s clothes in distress
62- Troubled, Nala leaves Damayanti sleeping alone and goes elsewhere
63- Damayanti’s lament; her life and chastity are protected from a python and a hunter; the hunter perishes due to Damayanti’s chastity
64- Damayanti’s lament and delirium; ascetics reassure her and she meets a group of merchants
65- Merchants are destroyed by wild elephants; sorrowful Damayanti lives happily in the palace of the king of Chedi
66- King Nala rescues the serpent Karkotaka from a forest fire; the serpent reassures Nala
67- King Nala becomes the chief charioteer at Rituparna’s court, constantly worrying about Damayanti, and converses with Jivala
68- The king of Vidarbha sends Brahmins in search of Nala and Damayanti; Sudeva the Brahmin visits the Chedi court, ponders Damayanti’s qualities, and meets her
69- Damayanti returns to her father; sends Brahmins in search of Nala with her message
70- Parnada tells Damayanti news of Nala in disguise as Bahuka; Damayanti sends Sudeva with a message about her swayamvara to Rituparna
71- King Rituparna departs for Vidarbha; Varshneya reflects on Nala; Varshneya and Rituparna are amazed by Bahuka’s remarkable chariot-driving skills
72- Conversation between Rituparna and Nala about Rituparna’s garment falling and counting the fruits of the Baheda tree; Nala learns the secret of dice from Rituparna, Kali Yuga leaves Nala’s body
73- Rituparna enters Kundinapura; Damayanti’s thoughts; Bhima welcomes Rituparna
74- Dialogue between Bahuka and Keshini
75- On Damayanti’s orders, Keshini tests Bahuka; Bahuka, seeing his son and daughter, feels affection for them
76- Conversation between Damayanti and Bahuka; Nala reveals himself; Nala and Damayanti are reunited
77- After Nala’s revelation, a grand festival is organized in Vidarbha; Nala converses with Rituparna, who learns the science of horses from Nala and returns to Ayodhya
78- King Nala defeats Pushkara in dice and, after sending him to the capital, re-enters his city
79- The importance of reciting the tale of Nala; Sage Brihadashva reassures Yudhishthira, reveals the secrets of gambling and horsemanship, and departs

upaparvas.title: Tirtha-yatra Parva
chapters: 80- The Pandavas, along with Draupadi, worry about Arjuna
81- Sage Narada arrives to see Yudhishthira; upon being asked about the merits of pilgrimage, he introduces the dialogue between Bhishma and Pulastya
82- At Bhishma’s request, Pulastya narrates the greatness of visiting various sacred places
83- Description of the significance of many holy sites within the boundaries of Kurukshetra
84- The glory of various tirthas (holy places)
85- Description of the sanctity of Ganga Sagar, Ayodhya, Chitrakoot, Prayag, and other tirthas, and the greatness of the Ganga
86- Yudhishthira asks sage Dhaumya about holy forests, ashrams, rivers, and more
87- Dhaumya describes the tirthas of the eastern direction
88- Dhaumya describes the tirthas of the southern direction
89- Dhaumya describes the tirthas of the western direction
90- Dhaumya describes the tirthas of the northern direction
91- Sage Lomasha arrives, narrates to Yudhishthira about Arjuna obtaining divine weapons, and conveys Indra’s message
92- Hearing Indra’s and Arjuna’s message from Lomasha, Yudhishthira is pleased; he prepares for pilgrimage and sends back most of his companions
93- The Pandavas, after paying respects to the sages, set out for pilgrimage
94- Sage Lomasha, giving examples of gods and righteous kings, warns Yudhishthira about the harm of unrighteousness and assures him of the merits of pilgrimage
95- The Pandavas visit Naimisharanya, Prayag, Gaya, and hear of King Gaya’s grand sacrifices
96- The story of Ilvala and Vatapi, sage Agastya’s plan to marry for his ancestors’ salvation, and the king of Vidarbha giving a daughter to Agastya
97- Sage Agastya marries Lopamudra, does penance at Gangadwara, and departs to amass wealth for his wife
98- To acquire wealth, Agastya visits Shrutarva, Bradhnaśva, Trasadasyu, and others
99- Agastya approaches Ilvala for wealth, slays Vatapi and Ilvala, Lopamudra bears a son, and Parashurama regains lost radiance through pilgrimage
100- The gods, tormented by Vritra, acquire sage Dadhichi’s bones and make the Vajra weapon
101- Vritra’s death and the terrible counsel among the asuras
102- The Kaleyas destroy ascetics, sages, and students; the gods praise Lord Vishnu
103- At Vishnu’s command, the gods visit Agastya’s ashram and praise him
104- Agastya stops the Vindhya mountains from growing and travels to the seacoast with the gods
105- Agastya drinks up the ocean; the gods slay the Kaleya demons and ask Brahma how to refill the sea
106- King Sagara performs penance for progeny and receives a boon from Shiva

107- Birth of Sagara’s sons, sixty thousand of whom are incinerated by Kapila’s anger; Asamanjas is abandoned; Anshuman completes Sagara’s sacrifice and inherits the kingdom, followed by Dilipa and Bhagiratha
108- Bhagiratha, through penance on the Himalayas, pleases Ganga and Shiva and receives their blessings
109- Ganga descends to earth and fills the ocean, redeeming Sagara’s sons
110- The glory of Nanda and Kausiki; the story of sage Rishyashringa and King Lomapada’s efforts to bring him to his kingdom
111- The courtesan entices Rishyashringa; sage Vibhandaka, worried, inquires about his son’s fate
112- Rishyashringa explains to his father the reasons for his concern, and describes the appearance and behavior of the courtesan in disguise
113- Rishyashringa visits King Lomapada, receives his daughter in marriage, the king welcomes Vibhandaka, who is pleased
114- Yudhishthira travels via Kausiki, Ganga Sagar, and the Vaitarani river to Mount Mahendra
115- Akritavrana narrates to Yudhishthira, in the context of Parashurama’s story, the marriage of sage Richika to Gadhi’s daughter and the birth of Jamadagni due to sage Bhrigu’s grace
116- At his father’s command, Parashurama beheads his mother and revives her by boon; Parashurama slays Kartavirya Arjuna, whose sons kill Jamadagni
117- Parashurama laments for his father, exterminates the Kshatriyas twenty-one times, and is worshipped by Yudhishthira
118- The Pandavas, after visiting many tirthas, reach Prabhasa and begin penance; the Yadavas meet the Pandavas
119- Balarama expresses his sympathetic sorrow for the Pandavas at Prabhasa tirtha
120- Satyaki’s courageous words; Yudhishthira agrees with Krishna’s advice and the Pandavas reside on the banks of the Payoshni river
121- Praise for King Gaya’s sacrifices, the significance of Payoshni, Mount Vaidurya, the Narmada, and the beginning of the Chyavana-Sukanya tale
122- Sage Chyavana obtains Sukanya
123- By the grace of the Ashvini Kumaras, Chyavana regains beauty and youth
124- At Sharyati’s sacrifice, Chyavana angers Indra and restrains the Vajra, creates Madāsura to slay him
125- Indra is freed from danger when the Ashvini Kumaras are granted participation in the sacrifice; Lomasha describes other important tirthas
126- The origin and brief story of King Mandhata
127- The story of Somaka and Jantu
128- Somaka has a hundred sons; both Somaka and his priest equally experience heaven and hell
129- The glory of the Plaksha Prasravana tirtha near Kurukshetra and the Saraswati tirtha
130- The greatness of various tirthas and beginning of the story of King Ushinara
131- King Ushinara offers his own flesh to protect a dove that sought his shelter from a hawk
132- The birth story of Ashtavakra and his journey to King Janaka’s court
133- Dialogue between Ashtavakra and the gatekeeper and with King Janaka
134- Debate between Bandi and Ashtavakra; Bandi is defeated; Ashtavakra’s limbs are straightened after bathing in Samanga
135- The glory of the Kardama region and other tirthas; the story of sages Raibhya, Bharadwaja’s son Yavakrita, and how Yavakrita died due to the rishis’ curse
136- Yavakrita’s adultery with Raibhya’s daughter-in-law; Yavakrita is killed by a demon born of Raibhya’s anger
137- Bharadwaja laments for his son, curses Raibhya, and enters fire himself
138- By the effect of Arvavasu’s penance, Paravasu is freed from the sin of killing a Brahmin, and Raibhya, Bharadwaja, and Yavakrita are revived
139- The Pandavas’ journey to Uttarakhand and Lomasha’s warning about its difficulties
140- Bhima’s enthusiasm and the Pandavas’ journey through King Subahu’s realm to Gandhamadana and the Himalayas
141- Yudhishthira expresses his mental anguish to Bhima for not seeing Arjuna and, recalling Arjuna’s virtues, resolves to go to Gandhamadana mountain
142- The Pandavas worship Ganga; Lomasha narrates the story of Narakasura’s death and the rescue of Vasudha by Lord Varaha
143- During the journey to Gandhamadana, the Pandavas encounter a storm
144- Draupadi faints; the Pandavas revive her; upon Bhima’s remembrance, Ghatotkacha arrives
145- With Ghatotkacha and his allies’ help, the Pandavas enter Gandhamadana mountain and Badrikashrama; description of the Badari tree, Nara-Narayana ashram, and the Ganga
146- Bhima sets out to fetch a Saugandhika lotus and meets Hanuman in the banana grove
147- Dialogue between Lord Hanuman and Bhima
148- Hanuman briefly narrates the story of Rama to Bhima
149- Hanuman describes the dharmas (virtues) of the four yugas
150- Hanuman displays his gigantic form to Bhima and explains the duties of the four varnas
151- Hanuman reassures Bhima and disappears after bidding him farewell
152- Bhima reaches the Saugandhika forest
153- The rakshasas named Krodhavasha question Bhima’s approach to the lake
154- Bhima defeats the rakshasas named Krodhavasha and collects Saugandhika lotuses for Draupadi
155- Witnessing a terrible omen, Yudhishthira and others worry and all reach the Saugandhika forest on Gandhamadana mountain to join Bhima
156- The Pandavas, following the divine voice’s command, return to the Nara-Narayana ashram

upaparvas.title: Jatasura-vadha Parva
chapters: 157- Jatasura abducts Yudhishthira, Nakula, and Sahadeva along with Draupadi; Bhima slays Jatasura

upaparvas.title: Yaksha-yuddha Parva
chapters: 158- From the Nara-Narayana ashram, the Pandavas travel via Vrishaparva to the ashram of royal sage Arstishena
159- Arstishena instructs Yudhishthira in the form of questions
160- The Pandavas reside at Arstishena’s ashram; at Draupadi’s request, Bhima ascends the mountain peak and, battling yakshas and rakshasas, kills Maniman
161- Kubera arrives at Gandhamadana mountain and meets Yudhishthira
162- Kubera counsels and consoles Yudhishthira and then departs for his abode
163- Dhaumya points out to Yudhishthira the peaks of Mount Meru and the abodes of Brahma, Vishnu, and others; he explains the motion and influence of the sun and moon
164- The Pandavas long for Arjuna, and Arjuna returns

upaparvas.title: Nivatakavacha-yuddha Parva
chapters: 165- Arjuna arrives at Gandhamadana mountain and reunites with his brothers
166- Indra visits the Pandavas, consoles Yudhishthira, and returns to heaven
167- Arjuna narrates his journey of penance, his battle with Lord Shiva, and the story of receiving the Pashupata weapon
168- Arjuna describes his training in celestial weapons in heaven and preparations for the battle with the Nivatakavacha demons
169- Arjuna enters the netherworld and begins battle with the Nivatakavachas
170- Arjuna and the Nivatakavachas engage in battle
171- Description of the demons’ illusory warfare
172- The destruction of the Nivatakavachas
173- Arjuna slays the Paulomas and Kalakeyas of Hiranyapura; Indra congratulates Arjuna
174- After hearing Arjuna’s account, Yudhishthira congratulates him and expresses a desire to see the divine weapons
175- Narada and others prevent Arjuna from displaying the divine weapons

upaparvas.title: Ajagara Parva
chapters: 176- Bhima’s conversation with Yudhishthira and the Pandavas’ departure from Gandhamadana
177- The Pandavas travel from Gandhamadana to Badrikashrama, Subahu’s city, and through Vishakhayupa forest, arriving at Dwaitavana on the banks of the Saraswati
178- Mighty Bhima kills wild beasts and is captured by a python
179- Conversation between Bhima and Nahusha in serpent form; Bhima’s distress and Yudhishthira’s search for him
180- Yudhishthira arrives at Bhima’s location and answers the questions posed by Nahusha in serpent form
181- Satisfied with Yudhishthira’s answers, Nahusha releases Bhima, regains his original form, and ascends to heaven after conversing with Yudhishthira

upaparvas.title: Markandeya-samasya Parva
chapters: 182- Description of the rainy and autumn seasons; the Pandavas re-enter Kamyaka forest from Dwaitavana
183- Krishna, sage Markandeya, and Narada arrive at Kamyaka forest; upon Yudhishthira’s inquiry, Markandeya discusses the consequences of actions
184- The greatness of ascetic and righteous Brahmins
185- Praise of Brahmins by sage Atri and King Prithu
186- Dialogue between sage Takshya and Saraswati
187- The story of Vaivasvata Manu and the tale of Matsya (fish) incarnation

188- The years of the four yugas and the effects of Kali Yuga; the vision of the dissolution of the world; Markandeya’s vision of child Mukunda, entering his stomach to see the universe, and their conversation
189- The child Mukunda reveals his form to Markandeya; Markandeya praises Krishna’s greatness and the Pandavas take refuge in Krishna
190- Description of the conduct during Kali Yuga at the end of the age and the advent of Kalki avatar
191- Kalki establishes the Satya Yuga and Markandeya delivers religious teachings to Yudhishthira
192- Ikshvaku dynasty king Parikshit marries the daughter of the frog king; the stories of Shal and Dal; the greatness of sage Vamadeva
193- Dialogue between Indra and sage Baka
194- Importance of Kshatriya kings; praise of Suhotra and Shibi
195- King Yayati donates a thousand cows to a Brahmin
196- The stories of Seduka and Vrishadarbha
197- Indra and Agni test King Shibi
198- Sage Narada proclaims the greatness of Shibi
199- The story of King Indradyumna and other immortal beings

200- Various topics: censured donations, censured births, worthy recipients of gifts, Brahmins who should or shouldn’t be invited to shraddha, characteristics of gift recipients, hospitality, importance of different gifts, purity of speech, Gayatri recitation, purity of mind, and self-control
201- Lord grants a boon to Uttanka for his penance and explains why Ikshvaku king Kuvalashva is called Dhundhumara
202- Uttanka urges King Brihadashva to slay Dhundhu
203- Birth of Brahma and the slaying of Madhu and Kaitabha by Lord Vishnu
204- Dhundhu’s penance and boon, Dhundhu’s slaying by Kuvalashva, and the gods grant Kuvalashva a boon
205- Greatness of a devoted wife and of serving one’s parents
206- The story of Kaushika the Brahmin and the devoted wife, describing the dharma of Brahmins
207- Kaushika goes to the righteous butcher; he is astonished to learn the devoted wife sent him, and the butcher explains varnashrama dharma, praises King Janaka, and describes proper conduct
208- The righteous butcher discusses violence and nonviolence
209- Subtlety of dharma, auspicious and inauspicious actions and their consequences, and methods for attaining Brahman
210- Harm from sense indulgence, benefit from good company, and description of Brahmi knowledge
211- Qualities of the five great elements and self-control
212- Nature and results of the three gunas
213- Description of the prana (life force) and ways to realize the Supreme Self
214- The importance of serving one’s parents
215- The righteous butcher instructs Kaushika on serving parents and narrates his previous birth and the reason for being born as a butcher
216- Conclusion of the Kaushika–righteous butcher dialogue and Kaushika’s return home
217- Agni accepts Angira’s first son as his own and Brihaspati is born from Angira
218- The descendants of Angira
219- The descendants of Brihaspati
220- Origin of the Panchajanya fire and its descendants
221- The fiery nature of Agni and the descendants of Bhanu (Manu)
222- The Agni called Sah enters the water and is brought forth again by Atharva Angirasa
223- Indra rescues Devsena from Keshi
224- Indra, with Devsena, goes to Brahma; visits the ashram of Brahma sages; Agni becomes infatuated and goes to the forest
225- Swaha meets Agni in the forms of sages’ wives; birth of Skanda (Kartikeya); Skanda splits the Krauncha and other mountains
226- Vishwamitra performs Skanda’s birth rituals; though urged by Vishwamitra, the sages do not accept their wives; Agni and others protect the child Skanda
227- Skanda grants protection to Indra and the gods who sought refuge
228- Description of Skanda’s attendants
229- Dialogue between Skanda and Indra; Skanda is consecrated as commander-in-chief of the gods and marries Devsena
230- The Krittikas are given a place among the constellations and various planets that trouble humans are described
231- Skanda honors Swaha Devi; Skanda, Rudra, and the gods journey to Bhadrawat; the gods and demons fight; Mahishasura is slain; Skanda is praised
232- The various famous names of Kartikeya and his praise

upaparvas.title: Draupadi-Satyabhama-samvada Parva
chapters: 233- Draupadi instructs Satyabhama on the duties of a devoted wife
234- Methods to please one's husband—serving him with utmost devotion
235- Satyabhama reassures Draupadi and departs for Dwaraka with Krishna

upaparvas.title: Ghosha-yatra Parva
chapters: 236- Upon hearing news of the Pandavas, Dhritarashtra expresses grief and anxiety
237- Shakuni and Karna praise Duryodhana and encourage him to visit the Pandavas in the forest

100- Krishna refreshes the horses, and after eating and resting, Arjuna attacks the enemy army again and advances toward Jayadratha
101- Seeing Krishna and Arjuna advance, the Kaurava soldiers are disheartened; Duryodhana comes to fight
102- Krishna praises Arjuna, encourages him; Arjuna and Duryodhana confront each other; Kaurava soldiers are frightened, and Duryodhana challenges Arjuna
103- Duryodhana and Arjuna fight, resulting in Duryodhana’s defeat
104- Arjuna engages in fierce battle with the Kaurava maharathis
105- Description of the banners of Arjuna and the maharathis; Arjuna battles nine maharathis alone
106- Battle between Dronacharya’s army and the Pandava army; Yudhishthira’s chariot is broken during battle with Dronacharya, causing him to flee
107- The deaths of Kshema, Veeradhanva, Niramitra, and Vyapradatta in the Kaurava army; Durmukha and Vikarna are defeated
108- Draupadi’s sons kill Somadatta’s son Shala; Bhima defeats Alambusha
109- Ghatotkacha kills Alambusha and the Pandava army rejoices
110- Battle between Dronacharya and Satyaki; Yudhishthira praises Satyaki and sends him into the Kaurava army to aid Arjuna
111- Dialogue between Satyaki and Yudhishthira
112- Satyaki prepares to go to Arjuna, is sent off with respect, and Bhima is sent to protect Yudhishthira
113- Satyaki battles Dronacharya and Kritavarma, then approaches the Kamboja army
114- Dhritarashtra’s sorrowful words; Sanjaya blames Dhritarashtra; Kritavarma fights Bhima and Shikhandi; defeat of the Pandava army
115- Satyaki defeats Kritavarma, kills Jigarati’s elephant, and kills Jalasandha
116- Satyaki’s valor; Duryodhana and Kritavarma are defeated again
117- Satyaki and Dronacharya battle; Drona is defeated and the Kaurava army flees
118- Satyaki kills Sudarshana
119- Dialogue between Satyaki and his charioteer; Satyaki defeats the forces of the Kambojas, Yavanas, and others
120- Satyaki destroys Duryodhana’s forces, causing Duryodhana and his brothers to flee
121- Satyaki slaughters the militia of stone warriors and Mlechchas; Dushasana flees with his army
122- Dronacharya rebukes Dushasana; Drona kills Virketu and other Panchalas and fiercely battles Dhrishtadyumna; Drona faints, Dhrishtadyumna flees, Drona wins
123- Satyaki’s fierce battle and defeat of Dushasana
124- Fierce battle between the Kaurava and Pandava armies and Duryodhana’s fight with the Pandavas
125- Dronacharya kills Brihatkshatra, Dhrishtiketu, Sahadeva son of Jarasandha, and Dhrishtadyumna’s son Kshatradharma; Chekitana is defeated
126- Yudhishthira, worried, sends Bhima to find Arjuna and Satyaki
127- Bhima enters the Kaurava army, destroys Dronacharya’s chariot with its charioteer, kills eleven sons of Dhritarashtra, and causes the army to flee with the remaining sons
128- Bhima defeats Dronacharya and other Kaurava warriors, throws Drona’s chariot eight times, roars before Krishna and Arjuna, and Yudhishthira anxiously ponders many things
129- Bhima fights Karna and defeats him
130- Duryodhana reproaches Dronacharya, who shows him the outcome of deceit and sends him back to battle; he fights Yudhamanyu and Uttamaujas
131- Bhima defeats Karna
132- Fierce battle between Bhima and Karna
133- Bhima and Karna fight; Bhima destroys Karna’s chariot with its charioteer and kills Dhritarashtra’s son Durjaya
134- Bhima and Karna fight; Bhima kills Dhritarashtra’s son Durdhara, and Karna flees
135- Dhritarashtra, regretful, describes Bhima’s strength and blames his sons; Bhima kills Durmarshana and four other sons of Dhritarashtra
136- Bhima and Karna fight; Karna flees; Bhima kills seven sons of Dhritarashtra and displays great valor
137- Bhima and Karna fight, Bhima kills seven brothers of Duryodhana
138- Fierce battle between Bhima and Karna
139- Another fierce battle between Bhima and Karna; first Bhima, then Karna wins; finally, Karna and Ashwatthama flee, wounded by Arjuna’s arrows
140- Satyaki kills King Alambusha and Dushasana’s horses
141- Satyaki’s extraordinary valor; Krishna informs Arjuna of Satyaki’s arrival, and Arjuna is relieved
142- Bhurishrava angrily challenges Satyaki; as Bhurishrava is about to behead Satyaki, Arjuna cuts off his arm
143- Bhurishrava reproaches Arjuna; Arjuna replies; Satyaki kills the fasting Bhurishrava
144- Reason for Bhurishrava’s insult to Satyaki and praise of the Vrishni heroes
145- Arjuna attacks Jayadratha; dialogue between Karna and Duryodhana; Arjuna battles Karna and defeats him; Arjuna fiercely battles all the warriors
146- Arjuna’s extraordinary valor and the slaying of Jayadratha, king of Sindhu
147- Kripacharya is wounded by Arjuna’s arrows; Arjuna is pained; Karna and Shalya fight, and Karna is defeated
148- Arjuna rebukes Karna and vows to kill Vrishasena; Krishna congratulates Arjuna and, showing him the dreadful scene of the battlefield, takes him to Yudhishthira
149- Krishna shares the news of victory with Yudhishthira, who thanks Krishna; Arjuna, Bhima, and Satyaki are congratulated
150- Duryodhana, deeply troubled, reproaches Dronacharya
151- Dronacharya responds to Duryodhana and sets out for battle
152- Duryodhana and Karna confer and the battle resumes

upaparvas.title: Ghatotkacha-vadha Parva
chapters: 153- Battle between the Kaurava and Pandava armies; duel between Duryodhana and Yudhishthira, ending in Duryodhana’s defeat
154- Pandava warriors attack Dronacharya, who slays many of them
155- Dronacharya kills Shikhandi; Bhimasena slays the Kalinga prince with blows and slaps, and kills Dhruva, Jayarata, and Dhritarashtra’s sons Dhrishtin and Durmada

156- Soma Datta battles Satyaki and is defeated; Ghatotkacha and Ashwatthama battle—Ashwatthama kills Ghatotkacha’s son, an Akshauhini of rakshasa soldiers, and Drupada’s sons, leading to the defeat of the Pandava army
157- Soma Datta is wounded; Bhima kills Balika, slays ten sons of Dhritarashtra, seven charioteers of Shakuni, and five brothers; Yudhishthira defeats Dronacharya in battle
158- Duryodhana and Karna confer; Kripacharya rebukes Karna, who insults Kripa in return

159- Ashwatthama prepares to kill Karna; Duryodhana persuades him otherwise; Pandavas and Panchalas attack Karna, who displays valor; Arjuna defeats Karna; Duryodhana asks Ashwatthama to slay the Panchalas
160- Ashwatthama reassures Duryodhana and, in battle with the Panchalas, destroys Dhrishtadyumna’s chariot and drives off his forces with great valor
161- Bhimasena and Arjuna attack; the Kaurava army flees
162- Satyaki kills Soma Datta; Dronacharya battles Yudhishthira; Krishna orders Yudhishthira to avoid Dronacharya
163- Torches light up the armies of both sides
164- Fierce battle between both armies; Duryodhana orders soldiers to protect Dronacharya
165- Battle between both armies; Kritavarma defeats Yudhishthira
166- Satyaki kills Bhuri; Ghatotkacha and Ashwatthama fight a fierce battle; Bhima fights Duryodhana, who flees
167- Karna defeats Sahadeva; Shalya kills Virata’s brother Shatanika and defeats Virata; Alambusha is defeated by Arjuna and flees
168- Shatanika defeats Chitrasena; Vrishasena defeats Drupada; battle between Prativindhya and Dushasana
169- Nakula defeats Shakuni; fierce battle between Shikhandi and Kripacharya
170- Dhrishtadyumna battles Dronacharya and kills Duhsana; Satyaki and Karna fight; Karna advises Duryodhana; Shakuni attacks the Pandava army
171- Satyaki defeats Duryodhana; Arjuna defeats Shakuni and Uluka; Dhrishtadyumna defeats the Kaurava army
172- After Duryodhana’s reproach, Dronacharya and Karna have a fierce battle; the Pandava army flees; Bhimasena rallies the troops and, with Arjuna, attacks the Kauravas
173- Karna defeats Dhrishtadyumna and the Panchalas; Yudhishthira is alarmed; Krishna and Arjuna encourage Ghatotkacha and send him to battle Karna
174- Ghatotkacha and his chariot battle Jatasura’s son Alambusha, whom Ghatotkacha kills
175- Description of Ghatotkacha and his chariot; fierce battle between Karna and Ghatotkacha
176- Alayudha enters the battlefield; description of his form and chariot
177- Fierce battle between Bhimasena and Alayudha
178- Fierce fighting between both armies; Ghatotkacha kills Alayudha; Duryodhana laments
179- Ghatotkacha’s fierce battle and his death at the hands of Karna with the Indra-given Shakti weapon
180- Pandavas mourn Ghatotkacha’s death; Krishna is pleased and explains the reason
181- Krishna explains to Arjuna why Karna did not use the Shakti on him; Sanjaya tells Dhritarashtra and Krishna explains to Satyaki
182- Dhritarashtra laments; Sanjaya responds; Yudhishthira grieves, and Krishna and Vyasa console him
183- Dhritarashtra’s remorse, Sanjaya’s response, King Yudhishthira’s grief, and its alleviation by Lord Krishna and sage Vyasa

upaparvas.title: Drona-vadha Parva
chapters: 184- Both armies, exhausted by sleeplessness, lie down to rest at Arjuna’s suggestion and return to battle after moonrise
185- Duryodhana reproaches Dronacharya, who responds with sarcasm
186- Pandava heroes attack Dronacharya; slaying of Drupada’s sons, Drupada, Virata, and others; Dhrishtadyumna’s vow and fierce fighting between both sides
187- Description of the battlefield’s terrible state and Nakula’s defeat of Duryodhana
188- Duels: Dushasana vs. Sahadeva, Karna vs. Bhimasena, Dronacharya vs. Arjuna
189- Dhrishtadyumna defeats Dushasana and attacks Dronacharya; Nakula and Sahadeva defend him; Duryodhana and Satyaki converse and fight; Karna and Bhima battle; Arjuna attacks the Kauravas
190- Dronacharya’s heroic deeds; the sages command Drona to lay down his arms; upon hearing of Ashwatthama’s death, Drona loses hope of life
191- Dronacharya and Dhrishtadyumna fight; Satyaki displays and receives praise for his valor
192- The chief maharathis on both sides fight; Dhrishtadyumna attacks; Dronacharya renounces his weapons, attains Brahmaloka through yogic meditation, and Dhrishtadyumna beheads him

upaparvas.title: Narayana-astra-moksha Parva
chapters: 193- Kaurava soldiers and commanders flee; at Ashwatthama’s inquiry, Kripacharya narrates the events of Drona’s death
194- Dhritarashtra’s question
195- Ashwatthama’s furious words and unleashing of the Narayana weapon
196- Hearing the Kaurava army’s lion-roar, Yudhishthira asks Arjuna the reason; Arjuna explains Ashwatthama’s rage and the dire consequences of killing a guru
197- Bhimasena’s heroic statements and Dhrishtadyumna’s justification of his actions
198- Satyaki and Dhrishtadyumna angrily exchange arrows; Bhima, Sahadeva, Krishna, and Yudhishthira intervene to pacify them
199- Ashwatthama releases the Narayana weapon; Yudhishthira laments; Krishna instructs the soldiers on how to save themselves; Bhima heroically faces the weapon’s attack

200- Krishna gets Bhima off the chariot and pacifies the Narayana weapon; Ashwatthama admits his inability to use it again; he defeats Shusharma, drives away Satyaki, Duryodhana, Kripacharya, Kritavarma, Karna, and Vrishasena, then kills princes of Malava, Paurava, and Chaudisha; Bhima and Ashwatthama’s fierce battle causes the Pandava army to flee
201- With the Agneya weapon, Ashwatthama destroys an Akshauhini of the Pandava army; Vyasa explains to the worried Ashwatthama why Krishna and Arjuna are unaffected, praising Shiva and Krishna
202- Vyasa further extols the greatness of Shiva and the merits of reading and listening to the Dronaparva

upaparvas.title: Karna Parva
chapters: 1- Hearing a brief account of Karna’s death, Janamejaya requests Vaishampayana to narrate it in detail
2- Dialogue between Dhritarashtra and Sanjaya
3- Duryodhana reassures the army; Karna’s role as commander and a summary of his battles and death
4- Dhritarashtra’s grief and the distress of all beings
5- Sanjaya tells Dhritarashtra about the chief heroes of the Kaurava side who were slain
6- Description of the main Pandava warriors slain by the Kauravas
7- Description of the surviving Kaurava warriors and Dhritarashtra’s fainting
8- Dhritarashtra’s lament
9- Dhritarashtra, lamenting, questions Sanjaya for a detailed account of Karna’s death
10- Ashwatthama is proposed as commander-in-chief and receives the appointment
11- Under Karna’s command, the Kaurava army marches to battle, forms the Makara formation; the Pandava army forms the Arthandrakara formation; the battle begins
12- Fierce battle between both armies; Bhimasena kills Kshembhuti
13- Fierce battle between both armies; Satyaki kills Vinda and Anuvinda
14- Draupadi’s sons Shrutakarma and Prativindhya kill Chitrasena and Chitra; the Kaurava army flees; Ashwatthama attacks Bhimasena
15- Fierce duel between Ashwatthama and Bhimasena; both faint
16- Arjuna battles the Samsaptakas and Ashwatthama
17- Arjuna defeats Ashwatthama
18- Arjuna kills Dandadhara and Danda, along with their elephants; their army flees
19- Arjuna destroys the Samsaptaka army; Krishna praises Arjuna’s valor and shows him the battlefield; the king of Pandya begins battle with the Kauravas
20- Ashwatthama kills the king of Pandya
21- Terrible, fierce battle between the Kaurava and Pandava armies
22- A massive elephant attack on the Pandava army; Pandavas defeat Pundra; kill the kings of Banga and Anga; destroy the elephant army, causing it to flee
23- Sahadeva defeats Dushasana
24- Fierce battle between Nakula and Karna; Karna defeats Nakula and slaughters the Panchala army
25- Yuyutsu and Uluka fight; Yuyutsu flees; Shatanika and Shrutakarma, sons of Dhritarashtra, and Sutasoma and Shakuni engage in fierce battle; Shakuni destroys the Pandava army
26- Dhrishtadyumna fears Kripacharya; Kritavarma defeats Shikhandi
27- Arjuna kills King Shrutanjaya, Sishirathi, Chandradeva, Satyasena, and other maharathis; destroys the Samsaptaka army
28- Yudhishthira fights Duryodhana, defeats him; both armies engage in fierce, unprecedented combat
29- Yudhishthira defeats Duryodhana
30- Satyaki and Karna battle; Arjuna destroys the Kaurava army; Pandavas are victorious
31- The Kauravas hold council at night; Dhritarashtra attributes victory to fate; Sanjaya blames Dhritarashtra; Karna and Duryodhana converse
32- Duryodhana asks Shalya to be Karna’s charioteer; Shalya strongly resists, but after being praised like Krishna, agrees
33- Duryodhana tells Shalya the story of Tripura; terrified devas, led by Indra and Brahma, praise Shiva
34- Duryodhana describes Shiva’s wondrous chariot to Shalya; Shalya relates Shiva’s destruction of Tripura and Parashurama’s boon to Karna
35- Shalya and Duryodhana converse; Shalya agrees to be Karna’s charioteer
36- Karna prepares for battle and converses with Shalya
37- Omens in the Kaurava army; Karna boasts, Shalya mocks him, and praises Arjuna’s valor
38- Karna announces rewards for anyone who can locate Krishna and Arjuna
39- Shalya speaks harshly to Karna
40- Karna rebukes Shalya and insults the people of Madra, threatening to kill him
41- Shalya tells Karna a story about a swan and a crow, praises Krishna and Arjuna, and advises Karna to surrender to them
42- Karna acknowledges Krishna and Arjuna’s prowess, yet, in arrogance, rebukes Shalya and recounts curses received from Parashurama and a Brahmin
43- Karna continues to berate Shalya with self-praise
44- Karna criticizes the people of Madra, including those in Madra and Bahika
45- Karna details the faults of the people of Madra and Bahika; Shalya replies; Duryodhana pacifies both
46- Kaurava army forms battle array; Arjuna attacks on Yudhishthira’s orders; Shalya lists Pandava heroes and praises Arjuna
47- Fierce battle between Kaurava and Pandava armies; valor of Arjuna and Karna
48- Karna slaughters many Pandava warriors, including Bhimasena’s son Bhanusena; Nakula and Satyaki fight Vrishasena; Karna attacks Yudhishthira

49- Battle between Karna and Yudhishthira; Karna’s fainting; Karna defeats and insults Yudhishthira, slaying thousands of Pandava warriors and turning the battlefield into a river of blood; Pandava maharathis devastate the Kaurava army and force it to flee
50- Battle between Karna and Bhimasena; Karna flees
51- Bhimasena kills six sons of Dhritarashtra in battle with Karna; Bhima destroys the elephant, chariot, and cavalry divisions; fierce fighting between both armies
52- Fierce battle between both armies; Kaurava army is distressed
53- Arjuna destroys ten thousand Samsaptaka warriors and their army
54- Kripacharya defeats Shikhandi and kills Suketu; Dhrishtadyumna is defeated by Kritavarma
55- Fierce battle of Ashwatthama; Satyaki kills Kartikeya; Yudhishthira leaves Ashwatthama and goes elsewhere

56- Duryodhana battles Nakula and Sahadeva; Dhrishtadyumna defeats Duryodhana; Karna slaughters Panchala warriors; Bhimasena slays Kaurava heroes and their troops; Arjuna kills Samsaptakas; Ashwatthama battles Arjuna and is defeated
57- Duryodhana encourages the soldiers; Ashwatthama vows revenge
58- Arjuna asks Krishna to take him to Yudhishthira; Krishna drives through the battlefield, narrating the events
59- Dhrishtadyumna and Karna battle; Ashwatthama attacks Dhrishtadyumna; Arjuna saves Dhrishtadyumna and defeats Ashwatthama
60- Krishna describes the valor of Duryodhana and Karna, encourages Arjuna to slay Karna, and extols the valor of Bhimasena

61- Karna defeats Shikhandi; Dhrishtadyumna, Dushasana, Vrishasena, and Nakula battle; Sahadeva defeats Uluka; Satyaki defeats Shakuni; Kripacharya defeats Yudhamanyu; Kritavarma defeats Uttamaujas; Bhimasena defeats Duryodhana, destroys the elephant army, and causes the enemy to flee
62- Attack on Yudhishthira by heroic soldiers
63- Kripacharya defeats Yudhishthira, Nakula, and Sahadeva; wounded, Yudhishthira returns to camp to rest
64- Arjuna defeats Ashwatthama and causes the Kaurava army to flee; at Duryodhana’s urging, Karna slaughters the Panchalas
65- Krishna and Arjuna entrust the battle to Bhimasena and go to Yudhishthira
66- Yudhishthira asks Arjuna in confusion whether he has killed Karna
67- Arjuna explains why he has not yet killed Karna and vows to do so
68- Yudhishthira, angry, speaks harshly to Arjuna
69- Arjuna, ready to kill Yudhishthira, is restrained by Krishna, who tells him the story of Bhalaka and the sage Kashika, explaining the essence of dharma
70- Krishna saves Arjuna from breaking his vow, fratricide, and suicide; consoles and restores Yudhishthira
71- Krishna instructs Arjuna; Arjuna and Yudhishthira reconcile; Arjuna vows to kill Karna; Yudhishthira blesses him
72- Krishna and Arjuna set out for battle, encounter auspicious omens, and Krishna encourages Arjuna
73- Praising Arjuna’s strength and recalling the valor of Bhishma and Drona, Krishna reminds Arjuna of the injustice of Karna and Duryodhana, urging him to slay Karna
74- Arjuna’s heroic words
75- Fierce fighting between both armies; Sushena is slain
76- Bhimasena converses with his charioteer Vishoka
77- Arjuna and Bhimasena slaughter the Kaurava army; Bhima defeats Shakuni; Dhritarashtra’s sons flee to Karna
78- Karna slaughters the Pandava army, forcing them to flee

79- Arjuna destroys the Kaurava army, creating a river of blood, and asks Krishna to move the chariot toward Karna; seeing Krishna and Arjuna, Shalya and Karna converse; Arjuna devastates the Kaurava army
80- Arjuna destroys the Kaurava army and advances
81- Arjuna and Bhimasena slaughter Kaurava warriors; Karna displays valor
82- Satyaki kills Prasena; Karna displays prowess; Dushasana and Bhima battle
83- Bhima drinks Dushasana’s blood and kills him; Yudhamanyu kills Chitrasena; Bhima rejoices
84- Bhima kills ten sons of Dhritarashtra; Karna is frightened; Shalya consoles him; Nakula and Vrishasena battle
85- Kaurava warriors slay the sons of Kulinda and elephants; Arjuna kills Vrishasena
86- Krishna and Arjuna discuss the upcoming battle with Karna; Arjuna faces Karna
87- Arjuna and Karna meet in a chariot duel; all beings are anxious regarding their victory; Brahma and Shiva declare Arjuna’s victory; Karna and Shalya, Arjuna and Krishna converse
88- Arjuna destroys the Kaurava army; Ashwatthama proposes peace to Duryodhana, who rejects it
89- Fierce battle between Arjuna and Karna; Kaurava warriors flee
90- Fierce battle between Arjuna and Karna; Krishna saves Arjuna from Karna’s arrow; when Karna’s chariot wheel gets stuck, he asks Arjuna not to shoot him
91- Krishna warns Karna and Arjuna slays him
92- Mourning among the Kauravas; Pandavas rejoice; the Kaurava army flees; Shalya consoles Duryodhana
93- Bhimasena kills twenty-five thousand foot soldiers; Arjuna destroys the chariot division; the Kaurava army flees; Duryodhana fails to stop them
94- Shalya surveys the battlefield; the Kaurava army flees; Krishna and Arjuna return to camp
95- The Kaurava army flees to its camp
96- Yudhishthira, seeing Karna slain, praises Krishna and Arjuna; Dhritarashtra mourns; the glory of the Karna Parva

upaparvas.title: Shalya Parva
chapters: 1- Hearing Sanjaya’s account of Shalya and Duryodhana’s death, King Dhritarashtra faints; upon regaining consciousness, Vidura consoles him
2- Dhritarashtra laments and asks Sanjaya to narrate events in detail
3- After Karna’s death, the Kaurava army flees in fear of the Pandavas; Bhimasena kills 25,000 infantry who confront him; Duryodhana rallies the soldiers for renewed battle
4- Kripacharya advises Duryodhana to seek peace
5- Duryodhana rejects Kripacharya’s advice and opts for war
6- At Duryodhana’s request, Ashwatthama proposes Shalya as commander; Duryodhana requests Shalya, who accepts
7- King Shalya’s heroic speech and Krishna encouraging Yudhishthira to slay Shalya
8- Both armies assemble on the battlefield; description of their remaining numbers
9- Fierce battle between both sides and flight of the Kaurava army
10- Nakula kills Karna’s three sons; intense battle between the armies
11- Shalya’s valor; duels between Kaurava and Pandava warriors; Bhimasena defeats Shalya
12- Terrible mace battle between Bhimasena and Shalya; Yudhishthira battles Shalya, Duryodhana kills Chekitana, Yudhishthira kills Chandrasena and Dhumrasena, then fights Shalya and the sons of Madra
13- Extraordinary valor of Madra king Shalya
14- Arjuna battles Ashwatthama; Panchala hero Suratha is slain
15- Fierce battle: Duryodhana vs. Dhrishtadyumna, Arjuna vs. Ashwatthama, Nakula and Satyaki vs. Shalya
16- Duels between Pandava and Kaurava soldiers; Bhimasena defeats Duryodhana, Yudhishthira defeats Shalya
17- Bhimasena kills Shalya’s horses and charioteer; Yudhishthira kills King Shalya and his brother; Kritavarma is defeated
18- Slaughter of Madra king’s followers and the Kaurava army’s rout
19- Pandava soldiers praise the Pandavas while conversing among themselves, blame Dhritarashtra, and note the Kaurava army’s flight; Bhima kills 21,000 infantry, and Duryodhana encourages his troops
20- Dhrishtadyumna kills King Shalya’s elephant; Satyaki kills King Shalva
21- Satyaki kills Kshemadhurti; Kritavarma battles and is defeated; Kaurava army flees
22- Valor of Duryodhana and intense battle between both armies
23- Seven hundred Kaurava charioteers are slain; intense, rule-bound battle between the armies; Shakuni’s deceitful tactics and defeat
24- In Krishna’s presence, Arjuna reproaches Duryodhana’s stubbornness and destroys the chariot army
25- Arjuna and Bhimasena destroy the Kaurava chariot and elephant armies; Ashwatthama and others search for Duryodhana; Kaurava army flees; Satyaki captures Sanjaya
26- Bhimasena kills eleven sons of Dhritarashtra and slaughters many divisions of the Kaurava army
27- Krishna and Arjuna converse; Arjuna kills Satyakarma, Satyashu, and Susharma with 45 sons and his army; Bhima ends the life of Dhritarashtra’s son Sudarshana
28- Sahadeva kills Uluka and Shakuni; Duryodhana flees with the remaining army

upaparvas.title: Gada-pravesha Parva
chapters: 29- The slaughter of the remaining Kaurava army; Sanjaya’s release from captivity; Duryodhana enters the lake; Yuyutsu returns to Hastinapura with the royal women

upaparvas.title: Gada Parva
chapters: 30- Ashwatthama, Kritavarma, and Kripacharya visit Duryodhana at the lake to discuss battle; upon learning his location from hunters, Yudhishthira arrives with his army and Kripacharya and others withdraw
31- The Pandavas go to the Dyutapayana lake; conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna, and Yudhishthira’s dialogue with Duryodhana, who is hiding in the lake
32- At Yudhishthira’s invitation, Duryodhana emerges from the lake and agrees to fight a single Pandava in mace combat
33- Krishna rebukes Yudhishthira, praises Bhimasena, and the mace duel between Bhima and Duryodhana begins
34- Arrival and welcome of Balarama; the battle between Bhima and Duryodhana commences
35- Balarama’s pilgrimage; during the description of Prabhasa Kshetra’s glory, the story of the moon’s liberation from a curse
36- Origin of the Udapana Tirtha; the story of sage Trita falling into a well, performing a yajna, and cursing his brothers
37- Balarama visits various tirthas: Vinashana, Subhumika, Gandharva, Gargasita, Shankha, Daitavana, Naimisha, and then enters the Saptasarasvati Tirtha
38- Origin and glory of Saptasarasvati Tirtha and the story of sage Mankanaka
39- Stories of Ushanas and Kapalamochana Tirtha, and the glory of the Purnodaka Tirtha at Karna’s hermitage
40- Asceticism and boon of Arshishena and Vishramika
41- The story of Duly, his sacrifice, and the description of Yayati’s yuga, during the narration of the glory of Avakiirna and Yayati Tirtha
42- The wrath of Vishwamitra and Vasishta’s forbearance during the origin story of Vasishta-apavaha Tirtha
43- The sages remove Sarasvati’s curse, purify the water, and relieve the crisis of rakshasas and Indra at Arunasangama
44- Birth of Kumara Kartikeya and preparations for his consecration
45- Consecration of Skanda, description of his various forms and names
46- Introduction to the Matrikas; Skanda sets out for battle and slays Tarakasura, Mahishasura, and other demons
47- Consecration of Varuna, origin stories of Agnitirtha, Brahmayoni, and Kubera Tirtha

243- Description of householder dharma by highlighting Brahmins
