245- Conduct of a sannyasi, and praise of the wise renunciant
246- Supremacy of the Supreme Self, how to realize Him, and who is qualified for this knowledge
247- Analysis of the great elements and related principles
248- The superiority of intellect and the distinction between nature (prakriti) and soul (purusha)
249- Means of knowledge and characteristics of the wise
250- Means for attaining the Supreme Self; description of the river of worldly existence and attainment of Brahman through knowledge
251- Characteristics of a Brahmin who knows Brahman and means to attain the Supreme
252- Functions of the five elements in the body and identifying their qualities
253- Realizing the individual soul and Supreme Self as distinct from gross, subtle, and causal bodies through yoga
254- The wondrous tree of desire—how to cut it down for liberation—and description of the body as a city
255- Detailed description of the qualities of the five elements, mind, and intellect
256- Yudhishthira’s question about death; Narada narrates to King Akampana the origin of death, describing how Brahma’s fire of anger destroyed beings
257- Brahma, at Shiva’s request, quenches his fire of anger and death is created
258- Death’s severe penance and, at Prajapati’s command, her acceptance of the task of destroying living beings
259- Determining the nature of dharma and adharma
260- Yudhishthira expresses doubts about the authority of dharma
261- Intense austerity of Jajali; birds make nests in his matted hair; his pride is humbled by a heavenly voice that sends him to the merchant Tuladhara
262- Dialogue between Jajali and Tuladhara on dharma
263- Tuladhara instructs Jajali on the dharma of self-sacrifice
264- Jajali receives teachings from birds
265- King Vichaknu extols non-violence (ahimsa) as the highest dharma
266- The story of sage Gautama and Chirakari, praising careful consideration before acting
267- Dialogue between Dyumatsena and Satyavan, praising non-violent rule
268- Dialogue between Syumarashmi and Kapila, with Syumarashmi emphasizing the necessity of sacrifice
269- Dialogue between Syumarashmi and Kapila on the paths of action (pravritti) and renunciation (nivritti)
270- Syumarashmi and Kapila: describing the attainment of Brahman by the best means in all four ashramas
271- Story of a Brahmin and the cloud Kundadhara, showing the excellence of dharma and asceticism over wealth and sensual pleasures
272- Condemnation of violence in sacrifice and praise of non-violence
273- Four questions from Yudhishthira about dharma, adharma, renunciation, and liberation, and their answers
274- Description of the means of liberation
275- Dialogue between Narada and Asita-Devala on liberation from identification with the body
276- Dialogue between sage Mandavya and King Janaka on renouncing desires
277- Impermanence of body and world, and a son’s advice to his father on duties for self-welfare
278- Description of the nature, conduct, and dharma of a renunciant as taught by sage Harita
279- Means for attaining Brahman; beginning of the dialogue between Vritra and Shukra
280- Sanatkumara gives Vritrasura spiritual instruction leading to his supreme attainment; Bhishma resolves Yudhishthira’s doubts
281- Description of the battle between Indra and Vritrasura
282- The slaying of Vritrasura and Brahma’s division of the sin of Brahmanicide into four parts
283- Shiva destroys the Daksha sacrifice, creates fever out of anger, and describes its various forms
284- To appease Parvati’s wrath and sorrow, Shiva destroys Daksha’s sacrifice; Daksha pleases Shiva with the Shivasuhrnama Stotra, receives a boon, and the glory of this hymn is described
285- Description of spiritual knowledge and its fruits
286- Samanga describes to Narada his state free from sorrow
287- Narada instructs sage Galava on the path to supreme good
288- Arishtanemi instructs King Sagara on detachment and liberation
289- The story of Bhrigu’s son Ushanas and how he came to be known as Shukra
290- Start of the Parashara Gita: Sage Parashara instructs King Janaka on the means to supreme good
291- Parashara Gita: The inevitability of karmic fruit and benefit from virtuous deeds

292- Parashara Gita: Superiority of wealth earned by dharma, the importance of hospitality, the method to clear five types of debts, the glory of praising the Lord, and the great benefit from good conduct and service to elders
293- Parashara Gita: Primacy of service for a Shudra, the glory of association with the virtuous, and the importance of all four varnas observing their respective dharmas

294- Parashara Gita: Means of livelihood for Brahmins and Shudras, command to renounce blameworthy actions, rise of asuric qualities in humans and Shiva’s removal of them, and instruction to perform duties according to one’s dharma
295- Parashara Gita: Downfall of those attached to sense objects, superiority of ascetic strength, and command to steadfastly uphold one’s own dharma
296- Parashara Gita: The secret of the origin of varnas, attainment of higher varna through ascetic power, special and common duties of various varnas, excellence of good deeds and non-violent dharma
297- Parashara Gita: Instruction on various dharmas and duties
298- Conclusion of Parashara Gita: Answers to King Janaka’s diverse questions
299- Hamsa Gita: The swan-formed Brahman instructs the sages
300- Distinction between Sankhya and Yoga, and description of the nature, means, fruits, and effects of the yoga path
301- The means and fruits of yoga according to Sankhya-yoga
302- Dialogue between Vasishta and Karala Janaka: explanation of the perishable and imperishable, and liberation through their knowledge
303- Due to association with nature, the soul considers itself as the doer and enjoyer of various actions and is repeatedly reborn in various forms
304- Soul’s downfall due to defects arising from association with nature
305- King Janaka’s doubt about the perishable, imperishable, nature, and soul, and Vasishta’s answer
306- Description of yoga and Sankhya and liberation through knowledge of the soul
307- Nature of knowledge and ignorance, perishable and imperishable, prakriti and purusha, and the liberation of the discriminating person

308- Description of the perishable, imperishable, and supreme reality; examples of unity and diversity of the soul; who is qualified and unqualified for this knowledge; and conclusion of the Vasishta-Karala Janaka dialogue
309- A sage advises King Vasuman of the Janaka lineage on dharma
310- Yajnavalkya instructs King Janaka—explaining, according to the Sankhya doctrine, the twenty-four principles and nine types of creation
311- Description of the unmanifest, great principle (mahat), ahamkara, mind, the time-measurement of sense objects and creation, and the primacy of the mind among the senses
312- Description of the process of destruction
313- Description of adhyatma (spiritual), adhibhuta (physical), and adhidaiva (divine); qualities of sattva, rajas, and tamas
314- Description of the destinies of men of sattvic, rajasic, and tamasic nature and King Janaka’s questions
315- Discrimination between nature and soul and its fruits
316- Description of yoga and attainment of the Supreme through its practice
317- Results of the departure of life-forces from various limbs, signs of impending death, and ways to conquer death
318- Yajnavalkya narrates how he received Vedic knowledge from the sun, Vishvavasu is taught about unity of soul and supreme soul and the result—liberation, after instructing Janaka, he departs
319- Dialogue between Panchashikha and King Janaka on transcending old age and death
320- Sulabha enters King Janaka’s body to test him; Janaka accuses her; Sulabha refutes him with arguments and calls him ignorant
321- Vyasa cautions his son Shukadeva with instructions on renunciation and dharma
322- Asserting that one must inevitably experience the results of good and bad actions
323- Vyasa’s penance to obtain a son and his boon from Lord Shiva
324- The birth of Shukadeva, his sacred thread ceremony, study of the Vedas, and completion of his education
325- At his father’s command, Shukadeva goes to Mithila, is honored by the gatekeeper, ministers, and young women, and then becomes absorbed in meditation

326- King Janaka worships Shukadeva and, answering his question, demonstrates that after attaining the Supreme Soul in the brahmacharya stage, the other three ashramas are unnecessary; characteristics of the liberated soul
327- Shukadeva’s return to his father and Vyasa instructs his disciples in self-study
328- After the disciples leave, Narada visits Vyasa and urges him to recite the Vedas; Vyasa explains to Shukadeva the reason for not studying and introduces the 'pravaha' and other seven winds
329- Narada instructs Shukadeva on renunciation and spiritual wisdom
330- Shukadeva receives Narada’s instructions on good conduct and spiritual matters
331- Narada teaches Shukadeva about dependence on karma for results; Shukadeva decides to ascend to the sun-world
332- Description of Shukadeva’s ascension
333- Shukadeva attains the supreme state; Shiva consoles Vyasa, who is distraught with grief for his son
334- In Badarikashrama, Narada asks Lord Narayana, who declares the Supreme God as the highest object of worship
335- Narada’s vision of Shvetadvipa, description of its inhabitants, the story of King Uparichara, and the origin of the Pancharatra
336- At King Uparichara’s sacrifice, Brihaspati is angered at the Lord; sages describe the glory of Shvetadvipa and the Lord to pacify him
337- Story of King Uparichara’s downfall for partiality in sacrifice, his restoration by divine grace
338- Narada praises the Lord with two hundred names
339- In Shvetadvipa, Narada beholds the Lord, who reveals his forms—Vasudeva, Sankarshana, etc.—and tells of his future incarnations and the glory of hearing and reading this tale
340- Vyasa teaches his disciples the secret of the Lord’s instructions on pravritti and nivritti dharma as told to Brahma and other gods
341- Krishna explains to Arjuna the origins and glory of his names
342- Account of the early stages of creation, mention of many brief tales extolling Brahmins, reasons for divine names, and Narayana’s victory over Rudra in battle
343- Janamejaya’s question; Narada returns from Shvetadvipa to Nara-Narayana and describes the important sights there upon being questioned
344- Nara-Narayana praise Narada and describe the greatness of Lord Vasudeva
345- Through Varaha, the tradition of ancestor worship is established
346- Conclusion of the narrative about Narayana’s greatness
347- The story of the Hayagriva incarnation, the rescue of the Vedas, the slaying of Madhu and Kaitabha, and the glory of Narayana
348- The tradition of Satvata-dharma and the glory of exclusive devotion to the Lord
349- At the beginning of creation, Vyasa’s birth as Apantaratama, son of Sarasvati, and his powers
350- On Mount Vaijayanta, Brahma and Rudra meet and Brahma describes the greatness of the Supreme Being, Narayana
351- Dialogue between Brahma and Rudra, especially extolling Narayana
352- Narada prepares to narrate to Indra the story of an ascetic Brahmin who lived by gleaning
353- Description of the good conduct of a noble Brahmin in Mahapadma City and the arrival of a guest at his home
354- The guest describes the various paths to heaven
355- The guest praises the good conduct and virtues of the serpent king Padmanabha and encourages the Brahmin to visit him
356- Pleased by the guest’s words, the Brahmin sets out for the serpent king’s abode as instructed
357- The serpent queen welcomes the Brahmin, and after conversation, the Brahmin waits for the serpent king’s arrival
358- The Brahmin performs penance to see the serpent king; the king’s family requests the Brahmin to eat
359- The serpent king returns home, discusses dharma with his wife, and at her request, resolves to give audience to the Brahmin
360- The serpent king’s pride and anger are dispelled by his wife’s wise words, and he prepares to meet the Brahmin
361- The serpent king and Brahmin meet and converse
362- At the Brahmin’s request, the serpent king narrates wondrous events concerning the solar orb
363- The divine destiny attained by one accomplished through gleaning and gathering
364- After conversing with the serpent king and resolving to practice gleaning, the Brahmin takes leave
365- The Brahmin, after taking leave, is initiated into the vow of gleaning by sage Chyavana, pursues ascetic discipline, and the tradition of this story is described

upaparvas.title: Dana-dharma Parva
chapters: 1- To console Yudhishthira, Bhishma narrates the dialogue of Gautami the Brahmani, the hunter, the serpent, the main person, and Time.
2- Description of the lineage of Prajapati Manu; Aniputra Surbhani attains victory over death by following the dharma of hospitality.
3- Yudhishthira asks how Vishvamitra attained Brahminhood.
4- Description of the lineage of Ajameedha and the story of Vishvamitra’s birth and his sons’ names.
5- Mention of the dialogue between Indra and the parrot to show the superiority of devoted and compassionate men.
6- Description of the superiority of human effort over fate.
7- Description of the fruits of actions.
8- The glory of noble Brahmins.
9- The fault incurred by vowing to give to Brahmins and then not giving, and by robbing Brahmins—narrated through the dialogue of the jackal and the monkey; the glory of giving gifts to Brahmins.
10- Story of a Shudra and an ascetic Brahmin about the harm of instructing the unqualified.
11- Description of persons, women, and places where Lakshmi resides or does not reside.
12- Description of the fate of Kritchhani and Prayaschitta, and the story of Bhangasvana, which discusses how women experience more pleasure than men in union.
13- Instruction to abandon sins committed by body, speech, and mind.
14- By Bhishma’s command, Krishna narrates to Yudhishthira the story of Upamanyu’s praise and worship of Shiva, the vision and boon granted, and his own vision of Shiva.
15- Shiva and Parvati grant Krishna a boon and Upamanyu describes the greatness of Shiva.
16- Dialogue between Upamanyu and Krishna—saga Tandya’s praise and prayer to Shiva, and its fruit.
17- The Shiva Sahasranama Stotra and the fruits of its recitation.
18- The glory of reciting Shiva Sahasranama; sages describe their experiences of attaining desires by Shiva’s grace; Krishna praises the greatness of Shiva.
19- Sage Ashtavakra, on the advice of the generous sage, heads north; en route, Kubera welcomes him and he converses with the northern quarter, who appears as a woman.
20- Dialogue between Ashtavakra and the northern quarter.
21- Further dialogue between Ashtavakra and the north; Ashtavakra returns home and marries the generous sage’s daughter.
22- Yudhishthira’s various questions with dharmic answers; the characteristics of the best recipients for shraddha and gifts.
23- The qualities of those worthy of invitation for ceremonies to gods and ancestors, and the characteristics of those who go to hell or heaven.
24- Explanation of sins equivalent to Brahminicide.
25- Description of the glory of various holy places (tirthas).
26- The glory of Mother Ganga.
27- Story of Matanga, who performed penance for Brahminhood and converses with Indra.
28- Indra persuades Matanga to abandon his desire for Brahminhood and ask for another boon.
29- Matanga’s penance and Indra granting him a boon.
30- The battle between the sons of Vitahavya and the kings of Kashi; Pratardana kills them and, on Bhrigu’s instruction, King Vitahavya attains Brahminhood.
31- Narada describes the qualities of venerable persons and the benefits of honoring and worshipping them.
32- Royal sage Grishadarbha (or Ushinara) protects a refugee pigeon and attains the eternal world by that merit.
33- Description of the importance of Brahmins.
34- Praise of noble Brahmins.
35- Brahma describes the greatness of Brahmins.
36- Dialogue of Indra and Shambarasura about the praise of Brahmins.
37- Examination of recipients for gifts.
38- Apsara Panchachuda tells Narada about the faults of women.
39- Yudhishthira’s question about the protection of women.
40- Vipula of the Bhargava lineage protects his guru’s wife by entering her body through yogic power.
41- Vipula saves his guru’s wife from Indra and receives a boon from his guru.
42- Vipula, at his guru’s command, brings divine flowers and is reminded of his own lapse.
43- Deva Sharma absolves Vipula of blame, and Bhishma instructs Yudhishthira to protect women.
44- Various views regarding daughters’ education and the eligibility of recipients.
45- Explanation about the education of girls and inheritance rights of daughters and other heirs.
46- The necessity of providing women with ornaments and wealth.
47- Description of the division of property among Brahmins and other varnas.
48- Detailed account of the birth of offspring of mixed castes.
49- Description of various kinds of sons.
50- In the context of the glory of cows, the story of sage Vyavana: the sage, trapped with fish in a net, comes out of the water.
51- King Nahusha buys sage Vyavana for the price of a cow; the sage describes the glory of cows, and the noble fate of fish and boatmen.
52- King Krishika and his queen serve the sage Vyavana.
53- Sage Chyavana tests the king and queen’s devotion and, pleased with their service, blesses them.
54- By the power of sage Vyavana, King Krishika and his queen witness many auspicious visions; sage Chyavana, pleased, invites the king to ask for a boon.
55- On Krishika’s inquiry, Chyavana explains why he resides in their home and grants them a boon.
56- Chyavana tells the reason for the connection between the Bhrigu lineage and the Krishikas, and departs on pilgrimage.
57- The fruits of various types of penance and charitable acts.
58- The merit of creating reservoirs and planting gardens.
59- Bhishma, praising great gifts and noble Brahmins, instructs on honoring them.
60- Special merit in giving to the best non-begging, virtuous, poor, and worthy people.
61- The king’s duty to perform sacrifices, give charity, and protect Brahmins and subjects.
62- The supreme importance of land donation among all charities, and the dialogue of Indra and Brahma on the same.
63- The special greatness of land donation.
64- The merit of donating different items during various stars’ conjunctions.
65- The glory of giving gold, water, and other items.
66- The merit of donating shoes, clothing, sesame, land, ghee, and incense.
67- The glory of giving incense and water.
68- The merit of donating sesame, water, lamps, and gems—dialogue between Yudhishthira and a Brahmin.
69- The glory of gifting cows and the merit gained by protecting cows and Brahmins.
70- The story of King Nriga as an example of the harm in stealing Brahmins’ wealth.
71- Nachiketa, cursed by his father, goes to Yama, who explains to him the glory of cow donation.
72- The worlds of cows and Yudhishthira and Indra’s questions about cow donation.
73- Brahma tells Indra the glory of Goloka and cow donation.
74- The faults of gifting or selling stolen cows, the dire results of cow slaughter, and the greatness of cow and gold donation.
75- The importance of vows, self-control, truth, celibacy, and service to parents, teachers, and elders.
76- The procedure for donating cows, prayers to cows, their resolve, and the names of kings who donated cows.
77- The origin and glory of Kapila cows.
78- Vasishta teaches Saudasa the procedure and glory of cow donation.
79- The fulfillment of desires by cows through penance and the greatness of giving cows; description of attaining higher worlds by donating different types of cows.
80- The glory of cows and cow donation.
81- The merit of ghee and Vyasa’s description to Shukadeva of the glory of ghee, Goloka, and cow donation.
82- Dialogue between Lakshmi and the cows: at Lakshmi’s request, cows grant her a place in cow dung and urine.
83- Brahma tells Indra the supremacy of Goloka and cows, and grants them boons.

84- Bhishma places the offering for his father Shantanu on kusa grass instead of in hand; the dialogue of Visphu and Prashushrama about the origin and greatness of gold donation; Parvati curses the gods, who, terrified by Tarakasura, seek shelter with Brahma.

85- Brahma reassures the gods; Animi searches, and by the power of Shiva, Ganga leaves the burning energy on Mount Meru; the birth of Kartikeya and gold; Shiva in the form of Varuna at the sacrifice, appearance of Prajapatis and gold, and Kartikeya slays Tarakasura.
86- The birth, upbringing, and appointment of Kartikeya as commander of the gods; his slaying of Tarakasura.
87- The fruits of performing shraddha on various lunar dates.
88- Description of forms assumed by ancestors during shraddha.
89- The fruits of performing shraddha during various constellations.
90- Examination of shraddha priests, the distinction between Panktidhvaja and Panktipavana priests, and the superiority of feeding a single Vedic scholar over thousands of ignorant priests.
91- Offering pindas for a bereaved mother’s son, advice of sage Agri, names of the Vishravas, and things to avoid in shraddha.
92- Unsatisfied ancestors and gods, their complaint to Brahma, the remedy by Amik, and blessings from satisfied ancestors after shraddha.

93- The secrets of householder’s duties; the story of Budhadharbi and the Sadarthis to illustrate the fault in accepting gifts; Indra, disguised as Brihaspati, slays Kritya and saves the Sadarthis; regarding the theft of lotuses, a hint at practicing dharma in the pretext of eating.
94- When lotuses are stolen at Brahmasar Tirtha, Brahmarshis and Rajarshis take oaths full of dharmic instruction, and at the advice of the wise, the stolen lotuses are returned.

95- The origin and glory of umbrellas and shoes; Yudhishthira’s question about gifts; due to the blazing sun, Renuka’s head and feet are scorched, Jamadagni is angered at the sun (in Brahmin disguise) and converses with him.
96- The origin and praise of umbrellas and shoes as gifts.
97- The duties of a householder and the five daily sacrifices—dialogue between Prithu and Krishna.
98- Dialogue between the ascetic Suvarna and Manu—the glory of gifts of flowers, incense, lamps, and offerings.
99- Nahusha’s oppression of sages and the conversation of Bhrigu and Agastya to remedy it.
100- Nahusha’s downfall, Shatakratu’s reinstatement as Indra, and the glory of giving lamps.
101- Dialogue between a Kshatriya and a Chandala on the faults incurred by stealing Brahmins’ wealth, and how the Chandala attains liberation by sacrificing his life to protect Brahmin property.
102- Dialogue between Dhritarashtra-disguised Indra and the virtuous Brahmin, explaining attainment of different worlds according to different actions.
103- Dialogue between Brahma and Bhagiratha, extolling the special merit of fasting even over sacrifice, penance, and charity.
104- Detailed explanation of the duties of householders, describing auspicious and inauspicious actions that increase or decrease lifespan.
105- Description of relationships between elder and younger brothers, and the honor of parents, teachers, and elders in the family.
106- Description of the fruits of various fasts related to months, fortnights, and lunar dates.
107- Special merit of fasts that yield the result of sacrifice for the poor, and detailed description of their fruits.
108- The greatness of mental and physical pilgrimages.
109- Special merit of fasting on the twelfth lunar day of every month and worshipping Lord Vishnu.
110- Observing Chandrabrata in Margashirsha for beauty and popularity.
111- Brihaspati tells Yudhishthira about the types of birth of living beings, the suffering of hell and animal births due to various sins.
112- Remedies for sins and the special merit of offering incense.
113- Brihaspati instructs Yudhishthira on the glory of non-violence and dharma, then departs for heaven.
114- Strong condemnation of violence and meat-eating.
115- The great fault of consuming liquor and meat, their renunciation, and the supreme benefit of abstinence.
116- The benefits of abstaining from meat and the praise of non-violence.
117- A worm remembers its previous birth due to good deeds, describes fear and happiness even in worm form, and asks for a means of welfare.
118- The worm is successively reborn in various animal forms, meets Vyasa, who grants it a boon to be reborn as a Brahmin and attain heavenly and eternal joy.
119- The worm is reborn in a Brahmin family, goes to Brahmaloka, and attains the eternal Brahman.
120- Dialogue between Vyasa and Maitreya—praise of charity and the secret of karma.
121- Vyasa and Maitreya discuss the merit of righteous and well-behaved Brahmins.
122- Vyasa and Maitreya discuss the glory of penance and the best duties of a householder.
123- Dialogue between Shandili and Sumana—description of the duties of chaste women.
124- Narada instructs Purushika on the worship of Lord Narayana and attainment of divine status; praises Samagupa; explains to a Brahmin the reason for a demon’s white and weak appearance.

125- Related to shraddha: dialogues between messenger gods and ancestors; sage Vishuddha and Indra on penance for sins; Indra and Brihaspati on dharma; and gods, sages, and ancestors on rituals for bull release, etc.
126- Dharma’s inner secrets described by Vishnu, Balarama, gods, Dharma, Animi, Vishvamitra, Gosamudaya, and Brahma.
127- Dharma’s secrets described by Animi, Lakshmi, Angiras, Gayarsha, Dhaumya, and Jamadagni.
128- Secrets of dharma and artha described by Vayu.
129- Secrets of dharma described by Tamas.
130- Secrets of dharma described by Arundhati, Yama (Dharmaraja), and Chitragupta.
131- The Pramathas narrate the secrets of dharma and adharma.
132- Secrets and influence of the twice-born regarding dharma.
133- Secrets of dharma narrated by Mahadeva (Shiva).
134- Secrets of dharma by Skanda, and the greatness of Lord Vishnu and Bhishma.
135- Description of those whose offerings should or should not be accepted.
136- Atonement for taking charity and consuming improper food.
137- Stories of kings who attained heaven by charity.
138- Description of five types of charity.
139- Sages visit ascetic Krishna, behold his glory, and converse with him.

140- Narada’s detailed description of Shiva’s glory on Mount Himalaya with spirits, Parvati’s arrival, Shiva closing his two eyes, the appearance of the third eye, the burning of the Himalayas, their restoration, and the initiation of Shiva-Parvati’s dialogue on dharma.
141- Shiva and Parvati’s dialogue on dharma—detailed explanation of varna-ashrama dharma and pravritti-nivritti dharma.
142- Uma-Maheshvara dialogue, description and glory of vanaprastha dharma and its observance.
143- Description of the primacy of auspicious and inauspicious actions in attaining Brahminhood and other varnas.
144- Description of auspicious and inauspicious actions by body, speech, and mind that result in bondage, liberation, heaven, hell, long, or short life.
145- Description of actions that lead to birth in high or low families, heaven and hell.
145-1- Description of royal duties.
145-2- Description of the duties of warriors and the glory of sacrificing one’s life in battle.
145-3- Brief description of royal duties.
145-4- Praise of non-violence and sense-control, as well as the supremacy of destiny.
145-5- Description of the three aims of life (trivarga) and auspicious conduct.
145-6- Description of various karmic results.
145-7- Description of the faults and diseases like blindness, lameness, etc., resulting from evil deeds.
145-8- Uma-Maheshvara dialogue on many important topics.
145-9- Description of the four types of beings, the secret of memory of previous births, the reason for rebirth through dreams, the discussion of fate and human effort, and the theory of rebirth.
145-10- Description of Yama’s realm, the paths there, the torments of sinners, and the births of yogis as per karma.

145-11- Description of the nature and fruits of auspicious and inauspicious actions (mental, verbal, physical), the faults of excessive indulgence, rules on pure diet, faults of meat-eating, benefits of abstaining from meat, compassion for living beings, procedure for worship of the guru, rules for fasting, brahmacharya, pilgrimage, merit of charity (incense, gold, ghee, land, daughter, knowledge), auspicious times and places, faults in gifts and dharma, different types of charity, worldly and Vedic sacrifices, and worship of gods.
145-12- Description of shraddha rites, the fruit of charity according to rules, the five fruits of charity, various dharmas and their results.

145-13- Description of the signs indicating auspicious and inauspicious destinies, the two types of beings in death, the four destinies of controlled beings, the great fruits of dying while performing one’s duty, and the attainment of hell by dying from lust, anger, etc.
145-14- Assertion of the supremacy of moksha-dharma, the means to attain moksha, and the primacy of detachment.
145-15- Explanation of Sankhya philosophy: origin of the twenty-four elements, etc.
145-16- Explanation of yoga-dharma and its fruits.
145-17- Description of Pashupata yoga and the glory of worshipping the Shiva lingam.
146- Description of stri-dharma (women’s duties) by Parvati.
147- Account of lineage and the glory of Krishna.
148- The glory of Krishna and Bhishma’s order to Yudhishthira to rule the kingdom.
149- The Vishnu Sahasranama Stotra.
150- Description of mantras suitable for recitation and the glory of chanting auspicious names of gods, sages, and kings in the morning, and the fruits of Gayatri recitation.
151- Description of the glory of Brahmins.
152- At Kartikeya’s sacrifice, Arjuna receives four boons from the fire-god, becomes proud, and the dialogue between Arjuna and Vayu on the glory of Brahmins.
153- By Vayu’s illustration, description of the greatness of Brahmins.
154- Description of the greatness of the foremost Brahmin Utathya.
155- Description of the greatness of sages Agastya and Vasishtha.
156- Description of the greatness of Atri and sage Vyavana.
157- When the demon Kapa takes control of heaven, Brahmins burn the Kapa demons; conclusion of the dialogue between Vayu and Kartavirya Arjuna.
158- Bhishma describes the glory of Krishna.
159- Krishna describes the glory of Brahmins to Prabrahma, recounts the story of Durvasa, and narrates the entire episode to Yudhishthira.
160- Krishna describes the greatness of Shiva.
161- The greatness of Shiva.
162- The supremacy of scriptural authority in dharma, the fruits of dharma and adharma, the characteristics of the noble and ignoble, and the essence of good conduct.
163- Yudhishthira asserts the primacy of destiny over knowledge, strength, and intellect; Bhishma responds.
164- Bhishma stresses that only auspicious and inauspicious deeds cause happiness and sorrow, and emphasizes adherence to dharma.
165- The glory of reciting the names of gods, rivers, mountains, sages, and kings daily.
166- With Bhishma’s permission, Yudhishthira departs for Hastinapura with his family.

upaparvas.title: Bhimatva-grahan Parva
chapters: 167- Bhishma, with funeral materials, is visited by Yudhishthira and others; Bhishma, after taking permission from Krishna and others to leave his body, gives final advice to Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira on their duties

168- Bhishma’s passing, his cremation by Dhritarashtra and others, the Kauravas offering water oblations to Bhishma in the Ganga, Ganga herself appearing and mourning for her son, and Krishna consoling her

upaparvas.title: Ashwamedhika Parva
chapters: 1- Yudhishthira, distraught with grief, collapses, and Dhritarashtra consoles him
2- Krishna and Vyasa console Yudhishthira
3- Vyasa advises Yudhishthira on how to obtain wealth for the Ashwamedha sacrifice, introducing the story of Samvarta and Marutta
4- Vyasa describes Marutta’s ancestors and narrates their virtues, powers, and wealth obtained through sacrifice
5- At Indra’s instigation, Brihaspati vows not to perform sacrifices for men
6- On Narada’s advice, Marutta follows the suggested method to meet Samvarta
7- Dialogue between Samvarta and Marutta; at Marutta’s earnest request, Samvarta agrees to perform the sacrifice
8- Samvarta instructs Marutta to worship Mahadeva by chanting his names to obtain gold; Marutta gains wealth, and Brihaspati is troubled by Marutta’s prosperity
9- Brihaspati tells Indra the reason for his concern; Indra sends Andhaka to Marutta with a message, but Andhaka returns, frightened by Samvarta, and tells Indra of the superiority of Brahmanic power
10- Indra sends Gandharva Raja to frighten Marutta, but Samvarta’s mind-power compels Indra and all the gods to attend; Marutta completes his sacrifice
11- Krishna narrates to Yudhishthira the history of Indra slaying the embodied Vritrasura
12- Lord Krishna instructs Yudhishthira to conquer his mind
13- Krishna emphasizes the importance of renunciation, mentions the Kama Gita, and encourages Yudhishthira to perform the sacrifice
14- The sages disappear; after performing shraddha for Bhishma and others, Yudhishthira and his brothers return to Hastinapura; description of Yudhishthira’s righteous rule
15- Krishna proposes to Arjuna that they depart for Dwaraka

upaparvas.title: Anugita Parva
chapters: 16- Arjuna asks Krishna about the subjects of the Gita, and Krishna narrates to Arjuna the dialogue of Siddha, sage, and householder
17- In response to questions, the Siddha Mahatma describes the various destinies of living beings
18- Description of the entry of the soul into the womb, conduct, inevitability of karma, and means to cross the world
19- In the dialogue of guru and disciple, the means of attaining liberation are explained
20- Brahmanhood—a Brahmin instructs his wife about knowledge
21- Description of a sacrifice performed by ten priests and the superiority of mind and speech
22- Description of the mind, intellect, and senses as the seven priests; dialogue between mind and senses
23- Dialogue of prana, apana, etc., and Brahma declares the supremacy of all
24- Dialogue between Devarshi Narada and Devamata, and description of the excellence of udana
25- Description of the Chaturhotra sacrifice
26- The supremacy of the Anya-rama
27- Description of the great forest of spiritual knowledge
28- The state of the wise man and the dialogue between Adhyar and Yati
29- The slaughter of the Kshatriya clan by Parashurama
30- Bhishma instructs Parashurama using the example of meditation yoga and Parashurama attains Indra by penance
31- The spiritual hymn sung by King Ambarisha about self-sovereignty
32- Dialogue between dharma disguised as a Brahmin and Janaka regarding renunciation of attachment
33- The Brahmin reveals his true, enlightened nature to his wife
34- Krishna concludes the Brahmin Gita while explaining to Arjuna the mystery of the brahmin, brahmani, and kshetrajna
35- Krishna explains moksha-dharma to Arjuna—questions and answers between Brahma and sages in the dialogue of guru and disciple
36- Brahma explains tamas (ignorance), its actions, and results
37- Description of the actions of rajas and the results of understanding it
38- Description of the actions of sattva and the results of understanding it
39- Description of sattva and other qualities, and the names of nature
40- The names of the great elements and the glory of knowing the Supreme Self
41- The origin of ahamkara (ego) and its nature
42- Creation of the five gross elements and senses from ahamkara; description of adhyatma, adhibhuta, and adhidaiva; teaching of the path of renunciation
43- Description of the rulers of all beings, the characteristics of dharma, and the means of experiencing objects; the peculiarity of the kshetrajna
44- Description of the beginnings and ends of all things and the eternity of knowledge
45- The wheel of time as the body and the duties of householder and Brahmin
46- Description of the duties of brahmachari, vanaprasthi, and sannyasi
47- Description of the means for liberation, the body as a tree, and the cutting of it with the sword of knowledge
48- Examination of the nature of the individual soul and the Supreme Self
49- The sages ask questions to determine the nature of dharma
50- The distinction between sattva and purusha, praise of the wise, detailed description of the qualities of the five elements, and the supremacy of the Supreme Self
51- The effect of penance, the nature of the soul, the glory of knowing it, and the conclusion of the Anugita
52- Krishna goes to Hastinapura with Arjuna, meets everyone there, then departs for Dwaraka with Subhadra and Daruka after taking Yudhishthira’s permission
53- On the way, Krishna hears the story of the destruction of the Kauravas from Utanka Muni, who becomes angry; Krishna pacifies him
54- Krishna explains spiritual truth to Utanka and explains Duryodhana’s wrongdoing as the cause of the Kauravas’ destruction
55- Krishna shows Utanka his universal form and grants him the boon of water in the desert
56- Description of Utanka’s devotion to his guru, his marriage to his guru’s daughter, and, on his guru’s command, his quest for the divine earrings from King Saudasa
57- Utanka requests the earrings from Saudasa’s queen, Madayanti, and is sent to her by Saudasa
58- Utanka’s return with the earrings, their theft on the way, and with the help of Indra and other deities, their recovery and presentation to his guru’s wife
59- Krishna arrives in Dwaraka and participates in a festival on Mount Raivataka, meeting everyone
60- On Vasudeva’s request, Krishna briefly narrates the events of the Mahabharata war
61- At Subhadra’s request, Krishna narrates to Vasudeva the story of Abhimanyu’s death
62- Vasudeva and the Yadavas perform shraddha for Abhimanyu; Vyasa consoles Uttara and Arjuna and instructs Yudhishthira to perform the Ashwamedha sacrifice
63- Yudhishthira consults with his brothers and sets out with everyone to fetch the treasure
64- The Pandavas reach the Himalayas, camp, and spend the night fasting
65- On the Brahmins’ advice, Yudhishthira worships Shiva and his family, digs up the treasure, and brings it back
66- Krishna arrives at Hastinapura, and Kunti requests him to revive the dead child of Uttara
67- Subhadra prays to Krishna to revive Parikshit
68- Krishna enters the maternity chamber, hears Uttara’s lament, and grants life to her son
69- Uttara’s lament and Krishna restores the dead child to life
70- Krishna names the child Parikshit and the Pandavas return near Hastinapura
71- Krishna and his companions welcome the Pandavas; the Pandavas enter the city, meet everyone, and Vyasa and Krishna instruct Yudhishthira to perform the sacrifice
72- On Vyasa’s command, Arjuna is appointed to guard the horse, Bhimasena and Nakula to guard the kingdom and city, and Sahadeva to look after the family
73- Arjuna follows the horse with the army
74- Arjuna defeats the Trigartas
75- Arjuna battles King Vajradatta of Pragjyotishpura
76- Arjuna defeats Vajradatta
77- Arjuna battles the Sindhus
78- Arjuna battles the Sindhus and, at Dushala’s request, ends the conflict
79- Arjuna’s battle with Babruvahana and Arjuna’s death
80- Chitrangada’s lament, Babruvahana’s grief upon awakening from a faint, and Arjuna’s revival by Ulupi with the Sanjeevani gem
81- Upon Arjuna’s inquiry, Ulupi reveals the reason for her arrival and Arjuna’s defeat; Arjuna bids farewell to his son and wife and continues after the horse
82- Defeat of Magadha king Meghasandhi
83- The horse enters Dwaraka, Panchanada, and Gandhara, passing through the southern and western coastal regions
84- Defeat of Shakuni’s son
85- Preparation of the sacrificial ground; visiting kings admire the arrangements and decorations
86- Yudhishthira instructs Bhimasena to honor the kings and Krishna relays Arjuna’s message to Yudhishthira
87- Conversation between Krishna and Yudhishthira about Arjuna, Arjuna’s return to Hastinapura, and the arrival of Babruvahana with Ulupi and Chitrangada
88- Babruvahana is honored with jewels and ornaments along with Ulupi and Chitrangada; the Ashwamedha sacrifice begins
89- Yudhishthira gives gifts to Brahmins and dismisses the kings with presents
90- At Yudhishthira’s sacrifice, a mongoose extols the merit of a handful of sattu (roasted barley) given by an ascetic Brahmin over the Ashwamedha sacrifice
91- Critique of sacrifices mixed with violence and of dharma
92- The story of sage Agastya’s sacrifice

upaparvas.title: Vaishnava-dharma Parva
chapters: 93- Yudhishthira asks about Vaishnava dharma, and Lord Krishna describes dharma and his own greatness
94- Description of the duties and fruits of all four varnas, means for the growth of dharma and destruction of sin
95- On futile birth, charity, and life; characteristics of sattvic donations; worthy recipients and the glory of Brahmins
96- Purity of seed and womb, the glory of Gayatri recitation and Brahmins, and the dire results of their disrespect
97- The sufferings on the path to Yama’s realm and ways to avoid them
98- The greatness of offering water, food, and hospitality
99- The glory of land donation, sesame donation, and the greatness of an excellent Brahmin
100- The greatness of various kinds of donations
101- The five great yajnas, proper bathing and its related rituals, favorite flowers of the Lord, and the qualities of devotees
102- The greatness of the Kapila cow and its donation, and the ten types of Kapila cows
103- Description of the dwelling of gods within the Kapila cow, its greatness, unworthy Brahmins, sins leading to hell, and merits leading to heaven
104- The sin equal to Brahminicide, praise of rice donation, description of those whose offerings are forbidden, the fruits of charity, and praise of dharma
105- The characteristics of dharma and cleanliness, instructions on honoring sannyasis and guests, good conduct, praise of donor Brahmins, and food donation
106- The proper method of eating, the rule for feeding cows grass, the glory of sesame, and the prohibition against Brahmins grinding sesame and sugarcane
107- Dharma in times of difficulty, characteristics of superior and blameworthy Brahmins, the best time for shraddha, and the essence of human duty
108- The nature of Agni, the procedure for agnihotra, and its glory
109- The method and merit of the Chandrayana vow as atonement
110- Description of universally beneficial dharma, the glory of the Dwadashi vow, and Yudhishthira's praise of the Lord
111- The glory of charity during Vishuvat and eclipses, the importance of the pipal tree, praise of sacred qualities, and superior atonement
112- Characteristics of good and inferior Brahmins, the greatness of devotees, cows, and the pipal tree
113- Conclusion of the Lord's teachings and his departure to Dwaraka

upaparvas.title: Ashramavasika Parva
chapters: 1- Yudhishthira and his brothers, along with Kunti and other queens, serve Dhritarashtra and Gandhari
2- The Pandavas treat Dhritarashtra and Gandhari with affection
3- King Dhritarashtra, wishing to go to the forest with Gandhari, requests Yudhishthira for permission; Yudhishthira and Kunti are saddened
4- On Vyasa’s advice, Yudhishthira grants Dhritarashtra permission to go to the forest
5- Dhritarashtra gives Yudhishthira instructions on statecraft
6- Dhritarashtra continues giving advice on statecraft
7- Dhritarashtra instructs Yudhishthira on political duties
8- Dhritarashtra seeks permission from the people of Kurujangala to retire to the forest
9- Dhritarashtra asks forgiveness from the citizens
10- On behalf of the people, the Brahmin Sambha gives a consoling reply to Dhritarashtra
11- Dhritarashtra asks Vidura to request wealth from Yudhishthira for performing shraddha; Arjuna agrees, but Bhimasena objects
12- Arjuna persuades Bhima and Yudhishthira agrees to give Dhritarashtra as much wealth as needed
13- Vidura conveys Yudhishthira’s generous response to Dhritarashtra
14- King Dhritarashtra performs shraddha for the deceased and a grand charity sacrifice
15- Dhritarashtra leaves for the forest with Gandhari
16- Dhritarashtra sends the citizens back, and despite the Pandavas’ requests, Kunti insists on accompanying him to the forest
17- Kunti responds to the Pandavas’ requests
18- The Pandavas and women return in disappointment, while Kunti, Gandhari, Dhritarashtra, and others reside on the banks of the Ganga
19- Dhritarashtra and others, after staying at the Ganga, move to Kurukshetra and reside at Shatayupa’s ashram
20- Narada increases Dhritarashtra’s zeal for penance by giving examples of ancient royal sages; on Shatayupa’s inquiry, he describes the destiny awaiting Dhritarashtra
21- The Pandavas and citizens worry about Dhritarashtra and others
22- The Pandavas worry for their mother; Yudhishthira desires to go to the forest; Sahadeva and Draupadi are eager to go too; Yudhishthira begins the journey with the royal women and army
23- The Pandavas travel with their army and reach Kurukshetra
24- The Pandavas and citizens meet Kunti, Gandhari, and Dhritarashtra
25- Sanjaya introduces the Pandavas, their wives, and other women to the sages
26- Dialogue between Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira; Vidura enters Yudhishthira’s body
27- The Pandavas visit the sages’ hermitages, distribute pots and other items, and then sit with Dhritarashtra; sage Vyasa arrives with other sages
28- Sage Vyasa inquires about Dhritarashtra’s well-being, praises Vidura and Yudhishthira’s righteousness, and asks them to request a boon

upaparvas.title: Putradarshana Parva
chapters: 29- Dhritarashtra mourns his deceased relatives; Gandhari and Kunti request Vyasa to grant them a vision of their dead sons
30- Kunti reveals the secret of Karna's birth; Vyasa consoles her
31- Vyasa introduces Dhritarashtra and others to their previous births, and, at his suggestion, everyone goes to the bank of the Ganga
32- By Vyasa's power, the Kaurava and Pandava heroes slain in the Kurukshetra war appear from the waters of the Ganga

33- The departed souls meet each other free from attachment and enmity, and at dawn vanish; at Vyasa's command, the widowed Kshatriya women bathe in the Ganga and attain their husbands' realms; the glory of hearing this Parva
34- Janamejaya asks how the dead could appear here in their former bodies; Vaishampayana explains
35- By Vyasa's grace, Janamejaya is granted a vision of his father
36- At Vyasa's command, Dhritarashtra and others bid farewell to the Pandavas, who return to Hastinapura with their retinue

upaparvas.title: Narada-gamana Parva
chapters: 37- Yudhishthira and others grieve after learning from Narada that Dhritarashtra and others were consumed in a forest fire
38- In Narada’s presence, Yudhishthira laments the burning of Dhritarashtra and others in the worldly fire, and the other Pandavas also weep
39- King Yudhishthira immerses the bones of Dhritarashtra, Gandhari, and Kunti in the Ganga and performs their funeral rites

upaparvas.title: Mausala Parva
chapters: 1- Yudhishthira sees evil omens, hears of the destruction of the Yadavas, and learns of the birth of the pestle from Samba’s stomach in Dwaraka due to the sages’ curse, and the strict command prohibiting alcohol
2- Seeing terrible portents in Dwaraka, Lord Krishna orders the Yadava clan to go on pilgrimage
3- Kritavarma and all the Yadavas destroy each other
4- Daruka goes to Hastinapura to inform Arjuna; Babhru passes away; Balarama and Krishna depart for the supreme abode
5- Arjuna arrives in Dwaraka and, seeing the state of Dwaraka and Krishna's wives, is grieved
6- Conversation between Arjuna and Vasudeva in Dwaraka

7- Vasudeva and the funeral rites for the Yadavas slain in the Mausala war; Arjuna leads the remaining men and women of Dwaraka away, the sea engulfs Dwaraka, bandits attack Arjuna en route, and the survivors are settled in his capital
8- Conversation between Arjuna and Vyasa

upaparvas.title: Mahaprasthanika Parva
chapters: 1- After performing the shraddha for the Vrishni clan and obtaining permission from the people, the Pandavas set out on their great journey with Draupadi
2- On the way, Draupadi, Sahadeva, Nakula, Arjuna, and Bhimasena fall one by one, and Yudhishthira explains the reason for each one's fall
3- Yudhishthira converses with Indra and Dharma, remains steadfast in his dharma, and ascends to heaven in his own body

upaparvas.title: Swargarohanika Parva
chapters: 1- Conversation between Narada and Yudhishthira in heaven
2- The divine messenger shows Yudhishthira the sights of hell; upon hearing the cries of his brothers, Yudhishthira resolves to stay there
3- Indra and Dharma console Yudhishthira, who then abandons his mortal body and ascends to the divine realm
4- In the celestial world, Yudhishthira meets Krishna, Arjuna, and others
5- Bhishma and other heroes return to their original forms; conclusion and the glory of the Mahabharata
6- The method of listening to the Mahabharata
7- The greatness (mahatmya) of the Mahabharata
